commands.name: GetPointFromUser
commands.description: Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled.

prompt.description: Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.

position.description: The clicked point in the project's coordinates.

example.description: Asks the user to click a point in the current window with GetPointFromUser and prints it. Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape cancels the input and the command fails.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to click a point in the current window with GetPointFromUser and prints it.

Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape cancels the input and the command fails.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPointFromUser', {'prompt': 'Click a point'}))

commands.name: ModelToScreen
commands.description: Converts model coordinates to pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. In a 3D window the coordinates are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded. Available from Archicad 29.

coordinates.description: Model coordinates in the current database (meters). In a 3D window they are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded.

screenPoints.description: One item per input coordinate, in the same order: the pixel position local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), or an error.

h.description: Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.

v.description: Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

example.description: Converts two model points to pixel positions of the current view window with ModelToScreen. The pixels depend on the window's size, scale and zoom. Requires Archicad 29 or later.

commands.name: ScreenToModel
commands.description: Converts pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window to 2D model coordinates of the current database, using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. It is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and several model coordinates can map to the same pixel.

screenPoints.description: Pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates).

h.description: Horizontal pixel position from the left edge of the view window.

v.description: Vertical pixel position from the top edge of the view window.

coordinates.description: One item per input screen point, in the same order: the 2D model coordinate in the current database (meters), or an error. This is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and in a 3D window the result is not a point of the model.

example.description: Converts two pixel positions of the current view window to model coordinates with ScreenToModel. The result depends on the window's size, scale and zoom.

commands.name: GetElementFromUser
commands.description: Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.

prompt.description: Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click. Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then.

elementTypes.description: Only an element of one of these types is accepted. A click on empty space or on an element of another type asks for the click again. Default: any element.

elementId.description: The clicked element. In a section or elevation window it is the model element the section element was cut from.

elementType.description: The type of the clicked element (one of the ElementType values, or Unknown).

position.description: The clicked point in the project's coordinates, as GetPointFromUser returns it.

elementPosition.description: The coordinate of the clicked part of the element (e.g. its node or hotspot), when Archicad gives one for it.

cancelled.description: True when the input was cancelled with Escape; no other field is returned then.

example.description: Asks the user to click a wall or a column with GetElementFromUser and prints its id, type and the clicked point. Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to click a wall or a column with GetElementFromUser and prints its id, type and the clicked point.

Waits for a click in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementFromUser', {
    'prompt': 'Click a wall or a column',
    'elementTypes': ['Wall', 'Column']
}))

commands.name: GetLineFromUser
commands.description: Waits for the user to input a line in the active Archicad window and returns start and end coordinates.

startPrompt.description: Prompt for selecting the line start point.
startPrompt.default: Click the start point of the line

endPrompt.description: Prompt for selecting the line end point.
endPrompt.default: Click the end point of the line

showRubberLineFeedback.description: If true, draws a unit-square rubber feedback around the cursor while input is active.

cancelled.description: True if the user cancelled the input (ESC).

startPoint.description: The start point of the line.

endPoint.description: The end point of the line. It is only valid if cancelled is false.

example.description: Asks the user to draw a line in the current window with GetLineFromUser and prints its end points. Waits for two clicks in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to draw a line in the current window with GetLineFromUser and prints its end points.

Waits for two clicks in Archicad; Escape returns cancelled.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLineFromUser', {
    'startPrompt': 'Click the start point of the line',
    'endPrompt': 'Click the end point of the line'
}))

commands.name: GetPolygonFromUser
commands.description: Waits for the user to input a polygon in the active Archicad window and returns its points and arcs.

startPrompt.description: Prompt for selecting the polygon start point.
startPrompt.default: Click the start point of the polygon

prompt.description: Prompt shown while placing the remaining polygon nodes.
prompt.default: Click polygon nodes and finish the input

method.description: Polygon input method. 'General' = free polygon, 'Rect' = axis-aligned rectangle, 'RotRect' = rotated rectangle, 'Polyline' = open polyline.

cancelled.description: True if the user cancelled the input (ESC).

example.description: Asks the user to draw a polygon in the current window with GetPolygonFromUser and prints its points and arcs. Waits for the polygon input in Archicad (a double click or Enter finishes it); Escape returns cancelled.
example.code:
"""Asks the user to draw a polygon in the current window with GetPolygonFromUser and prints its points and arcs.

Waits for the polygon input in Archicad (a double click or Enter finishes it); Escape returns cancelled.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPolygonFromUser', {
    'startPrompt': 'Click the first corner of the polygon',
    'prompt': 'Click the other corners, double click to finish',
    'method': 'General'
}))

commands.name: GetCurrentWindowType
commands.description: Returns the type of the current (active) window and, when it has one, the databaseId of the database it shows, which ChangeWindow takes to bring the window back after a script switched to another one. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned, as Archicad does not tell which one it was.

databaseId.description: The database shown in the current (active) window, the same id GetDatabases and GetContainingDatabases return. Pass it to ChangeWindow to bring this window back. Missing when the window has no database of its own that can be identified, for example a report, a rendering or a custom add-on window. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned: Archicad does not tell which one it was, and several saved views can show the same database.

example.description: Prints the type and the database id of the current window with GetCurrentWindowType.
example.code:
"""Prints the type and the database id of the current window with GetCurrentWindowType."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowType'))

commands.name: GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale
commands.description: Returns the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, as its denominator: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Unlike GetViewSettings it needs no saved view. It reads the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts always return 1.0.

scale.description: The denominator of the drawing scale of the current window: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Always 1.0 for layouts.

example.description: Prints the drawing scale of the current window (100.0 for 1:100) with GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale.
example.code:
"""Prints the drawing scale of the current window (100.0 for 1:100) with GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale'))

commands.name: SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale
commands.description: Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable.

scale.description: The denominator of the new drawing scale: 100 for 1:100, 20 for 1:20. Archicad accepts scales between 1 and 30000.

rebuild.description: Rebuild the window after the scale changed (the API's zoom flag). Default: false.

example.description: Sets the drawing scale of the current window to 1:50 with SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale, then restores it. Needs a window other than a layout (layouts are always 1:1).
example.code:
"""Sets the drawing scale of the current window to 1:50 with SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale, then restores it.

Needs a window other than a layout (layouts are always 1:1).
"""
import aclib

originalScale = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale')['scale']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale', {'scale': 50}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale', {'scale': originalScale, 'rebuild': True}))

commands.name: ChangeWindow
commands.description: Changes the current (active) window to the given window. A databaseId on its own is enough; the window type is taken from the database. The databaseId of a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened opens its Project Map item instead (from Archicad 27). With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan. windowType 'Report' on its own opens the Session Report window (from Archicad 26); its text cannot be read through the Archicad API.

example.description: Switches to the floor plan of the lowest story with ChangeWindow, then back to the window that was open.
example.code:
"""Switches to the floor plan of the lowest story with ChangeWindow, then back to the window that was open."""
import aclib

current = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetCurrentWindowType')
firstStory = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetStories')['firstStory']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'windowType': 'FloorPlan', 'storyIndex': firstStory}))

if 'databaseId' in current:
    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeWindow', {'databaseId': current['databaseId']}))

commands.name: GetContainingDatabases
commands.description: Returns the database (window type, database id and name) that contains each of the given elements, from any database, not only the current one. Pass the windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it, for example to find an element placed on a layout.

databases.description: The database of each element, in the order of the input elements. Pass windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it.

name.description: The name of the database (for example the name of the layout). Empty for databases without a name, like the floor plan.

example.description: Prints the database (window type, id and name) that contains each of the first two walls, with GetContainingDatabases. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Prints the database (window type, id and name) that contains each of the first two walls, with GetContainingDatabases.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:2]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetContainingDatabases', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: CloseWindows
commands.description: Closes the windows of the given databases (for example layouts, sections or details opened earlier with ChangeWindow), with one execution result per window; a window Archicad cannot close gets a failed result. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

databaseId.description: The database shown in the window, as GetDatabases, GetContainingDatabases or GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId return it.

windowType.description: Optional. When given, the window is only closed when its database is of this type.

example.description: Opens the first layout, goes back to the floor plan and closes the layout's window with CloseWindows. Needs at least one Layout. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: RebuildCurrentDatabase
commands.description: Rebuilds the current database, the one the API works on (see ChangeWindow). Requires Archicad 27 or later.

example.description: Rebuilds the current database with RebuildCurrentDatabase. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Rebuilds the current database with RebuildCurrentDatabase.

Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RebuildCurrentDatabase'))

commands.name: DeleteGhostRecords
commands.description: Deletes the trace (ghost) record of each given parent database, which removes the trace reference shown in that database's window. A database without a trace reference gets a failed execution result. Not undoable.

databases.description: The parent databases whose trace (ghost) record is deleted, as returned by GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId or GetContainingDatabases.

example.description: Deletes the trace reference (ghost) of the first section with DeleteGhostRecords. Needs at least one Section; one without a trace reference gets a failed result. Not undoable.

commands.name: GetUserGSID
commands.description: Get the current registered User-GSID and OrganizationsID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

userId.description: The stable GSID User ID of the logged-in user.

organizationIds.description: The list of organization IDs the user belongs to. Empty if not part of any organization or if the information cannot be retrieved.

example.description: Prints the Graphisoft ID of the signed-in user and their organizations with GetUserGSID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: ShowAlert
commands.description: Display a dialog with up to three buttons.

alertType.description: The type of the alert dialog.

title.description: The title of the alert dialog.

subMessage.description: Optional smaller sub-message text below the main message.

button2.description: Label for the second button (e.g. Cancel).

button3.description: Label for the optional third button.

clickedButton.description: Index of the button the user clicked: 1 = button1, 2 = button2, 3 = button3.

example.description: Shows a warning dialog with two buttons in Archicad with ShowAlert and prints which one was clicked. Waits until the user clicks a button.
example.code:
"""Shows a warning dialog with two buttons in Archicad with ShowAlert and prints which one was clicked.

Waits until the user clicks a button.
"""
import aclib

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ShowAlert', {
    'alertType': 'warning',
    'title': 'Tapir',
    'message': 'Some elements will be modified.',
    'subMessage': 'Click Continue to go on.',
    'button1': 'Continue',
    'button2': 'Cancel'
})

print ('Continue' if result['clickedButton'] == 1 else 'Cancel')

commands.name: GetSpecialFolders
commands.description: Retrieves the filesystem paths of the special folders of the running Archicad (preferences, cache, data, temporary, application, defaults, templates, help, embedded project library, etc.).

folderTypes.description: The types of the special folders to retrieve.

example.description: Prints the paths of Archicad's preferences, temporary and templates folders with GetSpecialFolders.

commands.name: GetEditModeState
commands.description: Tells whether Archicad is in a hierarchical editing mode (curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing), and which element is being edited. Read only: it never enters, leaves or cancels an editing mode. Commands that modify the project can fail while such a mode is active. The overall inEditMode flag requires Archicad 29 or later; the command requires Archicad 27 or later.

inEditMode.description: True when Archicad is in any hierarchical editing mode (curtain wall, stair, railing, beam, column, MEP elements, etc.). Only returned from Archicad 29.

example.description: Prints whether Archicad is in curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing mode with GetEditModeState. Requires Archicad 27 or later (the overall inEditMode flag needs Archicad 29).
example.code:
"""Prints whether Archicad is in curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing mode with GetEditModeState.

Requires Archicad 27 or later (the overall inEditMode flag needs Archicad 29).
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetEditModeState'))

commands.name: GetArchicadVisibility
commands.description: Returns whether the Archicad application is shown or hidden. Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.

isVisible.description: True when the Archicad application is shown, false when it is hidden.

example.description: Prints whether the Archicad application is shown or hidden with GetArchicadVisibility. Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
example.code:
"""Prints whether the Archicad application is shown or hidden with GetArchicadVisibility.

Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetArchicadVisibility'))

commands.name: SetArchicadVisibility
commands.description: Hides or shows the Archicad application, e.g. to keep it out of the way while a batch runs. A script that hides Archicad must show it again, also when the script fails (e.g. in a finally block). Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.

isVisible.description: True shows the Archicad application, false hides it.

example.description: Hides Archicad for two seconds with SetArchicadVisibility, then shows it again. Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
example.code:
"""Hides Archicad for two seconds with SetArchicadVisibility, then shows it again.

Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
"""
import time
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetArchicadVisibility', {'isVisible': False}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetArchicadVisibility')
time.sleep (2)

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetArchicadVisibility', {'isVisible': True}))

commands.name: RunActionCenterChecks
commands.description: Runs the given checks of the Action Center (by default the hotlink check). A successful result means the check ran, not that nothing was found: Archicad does not report the outcome to the caller, it shows the Action Center tab when the check found an issue.

checks.description: The Action Center checks to run, in this order. Omitted means ["Hotlinks"]. "Hotlinks" is available on every Archicad version; "All", "Libraries", "Drawings" and "Licenses" only on Archicad 25, later versions return an error for them in their execution result.

example.description: Runs the hotlink and library checks of the Action Center with RunActionCenterChecks. Archicad shows the Action Center tab when a check finds an issue; the result only says the check ran.
example.code:
"""Runs the hotlink and library checks of the Action Center with RunActionCenterChecks.

Archicad shows the Action Center tab when a check finds an issue; the result only says the check ran.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RunActionCenterChecks', {'checks': ['Hotlinks', 'Libraries']}))

example.description: Redraws the current database with RedrawCurrentDatabase.

commands.name: GetProductVersionInfo
commands.description: Retrieves the version information of the running Archicad: build number, language code, product family and version text, plus the product name, product type, main/update/hotfix versions, the available domains (Architecture, MEP) and the CEIP project identifier of the open project from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

productName.description: The name of the product. Archicad 29 or later.

productType.description: The Graphisoft product type. Archicad 29 or later.

productFamilyId.description: The identifier of the product family.

languageCode.description: The Graphisoft language code of the running Archicad (for example INT, GER).

buildNumber.description: The build number of the running Archicad.

versionString.description: The full version of the running Archicad as text.

mainVersion.description: The main version, as text. Archicad 29 or later.

updateVersion.description: The update version, as text. Archicad 29 or later.

hotfixVersion.description: The hotfix version, as text. Archicad 29 or later.

versionNumbers.description: The three parts of the version number. Archicad 28 only.

availableDomains.description: The domains available in the running Archicad. Archicad 29 or later.

ceipProjectId.description: The CEIP project identifier of the open project. Left out when no saved project is open. Archicad 29 or later.

example.description: Prints the build number, language, product name and version of the running Archicad with GetProductVersionInfo. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the build number, language, product name and version of the running Archicad with GetProductVersionInfo.

Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProductVersionInfo'))

cutawayEnabled.description: Whether 3D Cutaway is on in the 3D window.

cuttingPlanesVisible.description: Whether the cutting planes are shown in the 3D window.

example.description: Prints whether 3D Cutaway is on and the cutting planes are shown, with Get3DCutawayStatus. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
example.code:

commands.name: Set3DCutawayStatus
commands.description: Turns 3D Cutaway on or off and shows or hides the cutting planes in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.

cutawayEnabled.description: Turns 3D Cutaway on or off. Left unchanged when omitted.

cuttingPlanesVisible.description: Shows or hides the cutting planes. Left unchanged when omitted.

example.description: Turns 3D Cutaway on with Set3DCutawayStatus, reads it back, then restores the original state. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
example.code:
"""Turns 3D Cutaway on with Set3DCutawayStatus, reads it back, then restores the original state.

In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
"""

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('Get3DCutawayStatus')

    'cutawayEnabled': original['cutawayEnabled'],

commands.name: SetDialogAutoClose
commands.description: Turns the dialog auto close on or off. While it is on, Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user, so automation is not blocked by them. To have it on already while Archicad opens a project (before any command can be sent), set the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable to true for the Archicad process before starting it.

enabled.description: True turns the dialog auto close on: Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user. False turns it off.

example.description: Turns the dialog auto close on with SetDialogAutoClose, reads it back, then restores the original state. While it is on, Archicad closes its dialogs with their default button instead of waiting for the user.
example.code:
"""Turns the dialog auto close on with SetDialogAutoClose, reads it back, then restores the original state.

While it is on, Archicad closes its dialogs with their default button instead of waiting for the user.
"""
import aclib

original = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDialogAutoClose')['enabled']

commands.name: CreateHotlinkNodes
commands.description: Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node).

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink module nodes to create. A node that already points at the same source file (compared case-insensitively) is returned as it is, with existing: true, and the name and story settings asked for are ignored. On Archicad 25 a node that has not been placed yet cannot be found, so a repeated request there creates a second node.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the module source file (.mod or .pln).

name.description: Optional display name of the node. Defaults to the file name. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

storyRangeType.description: Optional. Which stories of the source are placed: all of them, or the single reference story. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

refFloorIndex.description: Optional index of the reference story in the source file. Defaults to 0. Ignored when a node for the same file already exists.

hotlinkNodes.description: One item per requested node, in order: the node guid with its existing flag, or an error.

example.description: Saves the first wall as a module in the temp folder, creates a hotlink node from it with CreateHotlinkNodes, then deletes the node. Needs at least one Wall.

commands.name: CreateHotlinkInstances
commands.description: Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring.

example.description: Places an instance of a hotlink node at (50, 0), rotated by 30 degrees, with CreateHotlinkInstances. The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Places an instance of a hotlink node at (50, 0), rotated by 30 degrees, with CreateHotlinkInstances.

The node is made from the first wall, saved as a module in the temp folder; at the end the node is
deleted with its instance. Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import math
import os
import tempfile
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
modulePath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), 'TapirExample.mod')
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SaveAsModuleFile', {'moduleFilePath': modulePath, 'elements': walls})
nodeId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkNodes', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'sourceLocation': modulePath}]})['hotlinkNodes'][0]['hotlinkNodeId']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateHotlinkInstances', {
    'hotlinkInstances': [{
        'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId,
        'origin': {'x': 50.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'rotationAngle': math.radians (30),
        'mirrored': False
    }]
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteHotlinkNodes', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': nodeId}]})

commands.description: Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content.

hotlinkNodes.description: The hotlink nodes to repoint at another source file, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. The placed instances stay where they are. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks on the same nodes to re-read the content from the new file.

sourceLocation.description: Absolute path of the new module source file (.mod or .pln).

example.description: Relinks the first hotlink node to a copy of its source file in the temp folder with ChangeHotlinkNodes, then back. Needs at least one hotlink whose source is a file on disk.
example.code:
"""Relinks the first hotlink node to a copy of its source file in the temp folder with ChangeHotlinkNodes, then back.

Needs at least one hotlink whose source is a file on disk.
"""
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import aclib

hotlinks = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotlinks')['hotlinks']
if not hotlinks:
    raise SystemExit ('No hotlink in the project.')
node = hotlinks[0]

copyPath = os.path.join (tempfile.mkdtemp (), os.path.basename (node['location']))
shutil.copyfile (node['location'], copyPath)

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeHotlinkNodes', {
    'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId'], 'sourceLocation': copyPath}]
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UpdateHotlinks', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId']}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotlinks')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeHotlinkNodes', {
    'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId'], 'sourceLocation': node['location']}]
}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UpdateHotlinks', {'hotlinkNodes': [{'hotlinkNodeId': node['hotlinkNodeId']}]})

"""Gets what the 3D window shows as a png with GetCurrentViewImage and writes it to the temp folder.

import tempfile

commands.name: SetElementUserData
commands.description: Stores string values under keys on elements, for scripts to keep their own state per element (external database ids, sync timestamps, markers). The data is saved with the project as the user data of the Tapir add-on on the element and appears nowhere in the Archicad UI. The given keys are merged into what the element already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. One undo step per call; in a Teamwork project the element has to be reserved.

elementUserData.description: The elements with the key-value pairs to store on them. Each item needs userData, keysToDelete or both.

userData.description: The key-value pairs to store on the element. A key that already exists on the element gets the new value; other keys are left as they are.

key.description: The key of the value. Scripts should prefix their keys (for example 'myscript.databaseId') so that different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

value.description: The value to store. Any text, for example an id, a timestamp or a JSON document the script encodes itself.

keysToDelete.description: The keys to remove from the element. A key the element does not hold is ignored.

executionResults.description: One result per input item, in the input order.

example.description: Stores a key-value pair on the first wall with SetElementUserData, reads it back, then removes it. The data is saved with the project, invisible in the Archicad UI. Needs at least one Wall.

commands.name: GetElementUserData
commands.description: Reads the values stored on elements by SetElementUserData: every key of each element, or only the given keys.

keys.description: Optional. Only the pairs with these keys are returned; a key an element does not hold is left out of its pairs. When omitted, every pair stored on each element is returned.

elementUserData.description: One item per element, in the input order: the pairs stored on the element (none when the element holds no user data of Tapir), or an error when the element was not found or its data could not be read.

userData.description: The key-value pairs stored on the element.

value.description: The stored value.

example.description: Prints the key-value pairs that scripts stored on the first ten walls (SetElementUserData) with GetElementUserData. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Prints the key-value pairs that scripts stored on the first ten walls (SetElementUserData) with GetElementUserData.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:10]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementUserData', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: CaptureElementState
commands.description: Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier.

type.description: How GetElementChangesSince finds the changed elements between this state and another one. ModificationStamp (the default) compares the modification stamps of the elements, so any change to an element counts. 3DModel compares the 3D model of the elements, so only a change that alters the 3D model counts, and capturing it generates the 3D model of the project. Two states can only be compared when they were captured with the same type.

stateId.description: The identifier of the captured state, accepted by GetElementChangesSince and ReleaseElementState. It is only valid in the Archicad session and project it was captured in.

type.description: The type the state was captured with.

example.description: Captures the current state of the project's elements with CaptureElementState. GetElementChangesSince can compare a later state to it. The script releases the state at the end.
example.code:
"""Captures the current state of the project's elements with CaptureElementState.

GetElementChangesSince can compare a later state to it. The script releases the state at the end.
"""
import aclib

state = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CaptureElementState', {'type': 'ModificationStamp'})
print ('Captured state: {}'.format (state['stateId']['guid']))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElementState', {'stateId': state['stateId']})

commands.name: GetElementChangesSince
commands.description: Returns the new, modified and deleted elements between a state captured by CaptureElementState and either another captured state (toStateId) or the current state of the project. Scripts that keep an external copy of the model use it to sync only what changed instead of re-reading every element. Fails for a stateId that is unknown - never captured, released, or lost because the project was closed or Archicad restarted.

stateId.description: The state to compare from, as returned by CaptureElementState.

toStateId.description: The state to compare to, as returned by CaptureElementState with the same type as stateId. If omitted, the current state of the project is used, so the response lists what changed since stateId was captured.

newElements.description: The elements that exist in the later state but not in the earlier one.

modifiedElements.description: The elements that exist in both states and changed between them.

deletedElements.description: The elements that exist in the earlier state but not in the later one. They cannot be read any more, only their identifiers are known.

example.description: Lists what changed since a captured state with GetElementChangesSince. Captures a state, creates a wall, reads the changes (the new wall), then deletes the wall and releases the state.
example.code:
"""Lists what changed since a captured state with GetElementChangesSince.

Captures a state, creates a wall, reads the changes (the new wall), then deletes the wall and releases the state.
"""
import aclib

stateId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CaptureElementState', {})['stateId']

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements']

changes = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementChangesSince', {'stateId': stateId})
print ('{} new, {} modified, {} deleted elements.'.format (
    len (changes['newElements']), len (changes['modifiedElements']), len (changes['deletedElements'])))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElementState', {'stateId': stateId})

commands.name: ReleaseElementState
commands.description: Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState. Every state is freed anyway when the project is closed or Archicad quits.

stateId.description: The state to free, as returned by CaptureElementState.

example.description: Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState with ReleaseElementState. States are freed anyway when the project is closed; releasing them earlier frees their temporary file.
example.code:
"""Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState with ReleaseElementState.

States are freed anyway when the project is closed; releasing them earlier frees their temporary file.
"""
import aclib

stateId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CaptureElementState', {})['stateId']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseElementState', {'stateId': stateId}))

commands.name: ChangeSelectionOfElements
commands.description: Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection.

example.description: Adds walls to the selection and removes one of them again with ChangeSelectionOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. The original selection is restored at the end.
example.code:
"""Adds walls to the selection and removes one of them again with ChangeSelectionOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall. The original selection is restored at the end.

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]

commands.name: FilterElements
commands.description: Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices) and element type (elementTypes). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter.

filters.description: Optional. Archicad's own flag filters. An element is kept only when it fulfills all of them.

layerIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when it is on one of these layers (the layerIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

floorIndices.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its home story is one of these (the floorIndex field of GetDetailsOfElements).

elementTypes.description: Optional. An element is kept only when its type is one of these.

example.description: Keeps only the editable walls and slabs of all elements with FilterElements.
example.code:
"""Keeps only the editable walls and slabs of all elements with FilterElements."""
import aclib

elements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllElements', {})['elements']

filtered = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FilterElements', {
    'elements': elements,
    'filters': ['IsEditable'],
    'elementTypes': ['Wall', 'Slab']
})['elements']

print ('{} of {} elements are editable walls or slabs.'.format (len (filtered), len (elements)))

commands.name: GetDetailsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the details of the given elements (geometry parameters etc). Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true.

fields.description: Optional filter for the fields to return for each element. When omitted, every field is returned. Fields not listed are not computed at all, so listing only what you need skips in particular the floorPlanPolygons extraction, which regenerates each element's 2D drawing primitives and can dominate the execution time of batch reads.

detailsOfElements.description: One entry per input element, in the same order as the input elements array. An element that cannot be read gets an error entry in its place, so the position of an entry tells which input element it belongs to.

oneOf.description: Details of an element. When the optional fields filter is given in the input, only the requested fields are present; the required list below applies to unfiltered requests.

hotlinkId.description: The hotlink instance this element belongs to. Present only for elements that came in through a placed hotlink; such elements are read-only.

floorPlanPolygons.description: Cut-fill polygons as drawn on the floor plan (wall joins resolved by ArchiCAD). Only collected for construction element types whose floor plan symbol comes from a real cut through the element - walls, columns, beams and their segments, slabs, roofs, shells, meshes, morphs, curtain walls and their segments/panels/frames, stairs and their risers/treads/structures. Absent for every other type, when the element has no cut fill, or when the floor plan database is not accessible.

oneOf.description: An element that is not in the current database but in another one (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...). Only the fields of its element header are returned: no id, details or floorPlanPolygons. Use GetContainingDatabases and ChangeWindow to open its database and read its full details.

hotlinkId.description: The hotlink instance this element belongs to. Present only for elements that came in through a placed hotlink.

fromOtherDatabase.description: Always true: the element is not in the current database.

example.description: Reads the details (type, story, layer, geometry etc.) of the first walls with GetDetailsOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. The second call asks only for the fields it needs, which is faster.
example.code:
"""Reads the details (type, story, layer, geometry etc.) of the first walls with GetDetailsOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall. The second call asks only for the fields it needs, which is faster.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': walls, 'fields': ['id', 'floorIndex', 'layerIndex']}))

commands.name: GetElementCategories
commands.description: Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status, Renovation Filter and, in the German version, BRI) with their possible values. The names of the categories and values are localized: identify a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name.

categories.description: The element categories of the project, each with its possible values.

name.description: The localized name of the category, for display only.

values.description: The possible values of the category.

name.description: The localized name of the value, for display only.

isVisibleOnUI.description: The value is offered in the settings dialogs of Archicad.

usableAsCriteria.description: The value can be used as a criterion, for example in Find & Select and in Graphic Override rules.

example.description: Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) and their values with GetElementCategories. The names are localized; scripts should pick a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId.

commands.name: GetCategoryValuesOfElements

categoryValuesOfElements.description: The category values of each element, in the order of the input. A category the element does not have is left out of its list; an element that does not exist or has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) is represented by an error object.

name.description: The localized name of the value, for display only.

if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

}))

commands.name: GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults
commands.description: Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the tool defaults of the given element types, the values new elements of the type get, optionally only for the given category types. A category the default has no value in is listed without categoryValueId; an element type without any of the requested categories gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

elementTypes.description: The element types whose tool defaults (the settings new elements get) are read.

categories.description: The categories to read. Left out: every category of the project.

categoryValuesOfDefaults.description: The category values of the tool defaults of each element type, in the order of the input. A category Archicad cannot read for the type is left out of its list; an invalid element type, or one with none of the requested categories, is represented by an error object.

categoryValueId.description: Left out when the default has no value in this category.

name.description: The localized name of the value, for display only. Left out when the default has no value in this category.

example.description: Reads the category values new walls, slabs and columns get from their tool defaults, with GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults.

commands.name: SetCategoryValuesOfElements

The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts.

elementCategoryValues.description: The category values to set: one element and one category per item. The same element can appear in several items, one per category.

categoryValueId.description: A value of the category given by type, as GetElementCategories lists them.

executionResults.description: One result per item of the input, in the same order.

commands.name: ConvertRevealOffsets
commands.description: Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27.

openings.description: Windows and doors placed in walls, each with exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset.

elementId.description: A window or door placed in a wall.

coreOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the core skin of the owner wall, to convert to the wall side reference.

sideOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the side of the owner wall, to convert to the core skin reference.

revealOffsets.description: The reveal depth offset of each opening in both references, aligned with the input, or an error.

coreOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the core skin of the owner wall.

sideOffset.description: Reveal depth offset measured from the side of the owner wall.

example.description: Converts a reveal depth offset of 0 measured from the wall's core skin to the wall side reference with ConvertRevealOffsets. Needs at least one Window or Door placed in a wall. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: Get3DGeometryOfElements
commands.description: Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while.

geometries3D.description: The 3D geometry of each element, aligned with the input: the solid bodies of its 3D model, or an error.

bodies.description: The solid bodies of the element's 3D model, including those of its subelements for a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of its segments for a Column or Beam. Empty when the element has no solid 3D model (for example a 2D element, or one filtered out of the 3D view).

example.description: Reads the 3D geometry (vertices and faces of the solid bodies) of a wall with Get3DGeometryOfElements. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Reads the 3D geometry (vertices and faces of the solid bodies) of a wall with Get3DGeometryOfElements.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""

commands.name: GetElementConnections
commands.description: Gets the connections among the given elements: each pair of touching elements once, with the polygons of the surface where they touch, in world coordinates. The 3D model of the elements is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. Also returns, aligned with the input array of elements, whether each element was found. Available from Archicad 28.

elements.description: The elements to search connections among. Only connections between two of these elements are returned.

connections.description: The connected pairs of the given elements. Each pair appears once.

polygons.description: The polygons of the surface where the two elements touch, in world coordinates. The last point of a polygon repeats its first.

executionResults.description: Aligned with the input array of elements: whether the element was found and taken into the search.

example.description: Finds where the walls and slabs of the project touch each other with GetElementConnections. Needs Walls or Slabs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Finds where the walls and slabs of the project touch each other with GetElementConnections.

Needs Walls or Slabs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

elements = []
for elementType in ['Wall', 'Slab']:
    elements += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': elementType})['elements']
if not elements:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall or slab in the project.')

connections = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementConnections', {'elements': elements})['connections']
for connection in connections:
    print ('{} touches {}'.format (connection['elementId1']['guid'], connection['elementId2']['guid']))

commands.name: GetBodyMaterialsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the building material of each body of the 3D model of the given elements. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.

bodyMaterials.description: The bodies of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

bodies.description: The bodies of the element's 3D model generated with separate components: a composite structure has one body per skin. Empty when the element has no 3D model.

bodyIndex.description: The index of the body in the element, starting from 0.

buildingMaterialId.description: The building material of the body. Left out when it cannot be found among the attributes of the project.

buildingMaterialName.description: The name of the building material. Left out together with buildingMaterialId.

commands.name: GetCutPolygonsOfElements
commands.description: Cuts each body of the 3D model of the given elements with a plane and returns, for each body, its building material, the area of the cut surface and its polygons (outline and holes) in 2D coordinates of the plane. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.

cutPlane.description: The cutting plane. axisX, axisY and axisZ should be unit vectors perpendicular to each other; axisZ is the normal of the plane.

basePoint.description: A point of the plane, the origin of the returned 2D coordinates.

axisX.description: The direction of the x axis of the returned 2D coordinates.

axisY.description: The direction of the y axis of the returned 2D coordinates.

cutPolygons.description: The cut of each body of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

bodies.description: The bodies of the element's 3D model generated with separate components: a composite structure has one body per skin. Empty when the element has no 3D model.

bodyIndex.description: The index of the body in the element, starting from 0.

buildingMaterialId.description: The building material of the body. Left out when it cannot be found among the attributes of the project.

buildingMaterialName.description: The name of the building material. Left out together with buildingMaterialId.

area.description: The area of the cut surface of the body. 0 when the plane does not cut the body.

polygons.description: The polygons of the cut surface of the body, in 2D coordinates of the plane (basePoint, axisX, axisY). Curved edges are given by their end points. Empty when the plane does not cut the body.

example.description: Cuts the first walls with a horizontal plane 1 m above project zero with GetCutPolygonsOfElements. Returns the building material, cut area and cut polygons of each body. Needs at least one Wall. On Archicad 25-27 the building materials are left out.

commands.name: GetElementAtCoordinate
commands.description: Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser.

elementType.description: The type of the element to look for. Only polygonal element types can be searched, for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch.

coordinate.description: The point to search at, in the project's coordinates, on the floor plan of the current database.

z.description: Optional. The elevation of the search point, handed to Archicad together with the coordinate. Default is 0; without z a point 1 mm higher is also tried, so an element whose top is at 0 (for example a slab at the story level) is found.

filters.description: Optional. Only an element passing every given filter is found (the same values as FilterElements accepts).

found.description: True when an element of the given type was found at the coordinate.

elementId.description: The identifier of the found element. Absent when nothing was found.

example.description: Finds the Slab at a point of the floor plan, the way a click there would, with GetElementAtCoordinate. The point is the average of the first slab's outline vertices. Needs at least one Slab.
example.code:
"""Finds the Slab at a point of the floor plan, the way a click there would, with GetElementAtCoordinate.

The point is the average of the first slab's outline vertices. Needs at least one Slab.
"""
import aclib

slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Slab'})['elements'][:1]
if not slabs:
    raise SystemExit ('No slab in the project.')

outline = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': slabs, 'fields': ['details']})['detailsOfElements'][0]['details']['polygonOutline']
point = {'x': sum (c['x'] for c in outline) / len (outline), 'y': sum (c['y'] for c in outline) / len (outline)}

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementAtCoordinate', {
    'elementType': 'Slab',
    'coordinate': point,
    'filters': ['IsVisibleByLayer']
}))

commands.name: GetSkylightHolePolygons
commands.description: Gets the polygon of the hole each given Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell: the outline and any holes of it as 2D coordinates. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element that is not a Skylight gets an error item.

skylightHolePolygons.description: The hole each Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell, aligned with the input: its polygon, or an error (for example for an element that is not a Skylight).

polygonOutline.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline of the hole, as Archicad returns them. The outline is closed implicitly (the first vertex is not repeated at the end); a curved edge is given by its end points only.

example.description: Reads the hole each Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell with GetSkylightHolePolygons. Needs at least one Skylight.

structureDisplay.description: The Partial Structure Display mode to check the elements in. The current window is not changed.

visibleSkinStatuses.description: Whether each element has a visible skin in the given Partial Structure Display mode, aligned with the input, or an error.

hasVisibleSkin.description: True when the element has at least one skin shown in the given Partial Structure Display mode.

absoluteBottoms.description: The absolute bottom of each element, aligned with the input, or an error.

absoluteBottom.description: The absolute bottom level of the curtain wall or its subelement, as returned by ACAPI_CurtainWall_GetCWAbsoluteBottom.

commands.name: GetQuantitiesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call.

minOpeningSize.description: Optional minimum opening size in square meters. Openings smaller than this are not subtracted when the conditional values (for example volumeConditional of a Wall) are calculated. Archicad only uses it for walls. Default value is 0, so every opening is subtracted.

calculateInOneCall.description: Optional. When true, Archicad calculates the quantities of all the supported elements in one call instead of one call per element, which can be faster for many elements. The output has the same format. If that one call fails, every supported element gets the same error. Default value is false.

quantitiesOfElements.description: The quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Lengths are in meters, areas in square meters and volumes in cubic meters.

composites.description: The quantities per building material, in the order Archicad reports them: one item for each skin of a composite or complex profile element, and a single item for a basic element. Empty for Zones and Morphs, for which Archicad reports no skins.

projectedArea.description: Projected area of the skin. Archicad reports 0 when the legacy intersection and surface calculation is turned on in the Project Preferences.

isCore.description: The skin is marked as core.

isFinish.description: The skin is marked as finish.

subElementId.description: The sub-element (for example a column or beam segment) the skin belongs to. Present only when Archicad attaches the skin to a sub-element.

example.description: Reads the quantities Archicad calculates (volumes, surfaces, lengths ...) of the first walls with GetQuantitiesOfElements. Openings smaller than 0.5 m2 are not subtracted. Needs at least one Wall.

    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetQuantitiesOfElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'minOpeningSize': 0.5
}))

commands.name: TriangulatePolygonsOfElements
commands.description: Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. With convex: true, the faces of the 3D model of the elements (of any type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, given by the 3D coordinates of their vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item.

convex.description: Optional. When true, the faces of the 3D model of each element (its own bodies, any element type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, as Archicad does it, and returned as convexPolygons. Default value is false.

triangulations.description: The triangulation of the polygon of each element, aligned with the input: its triangles (or with convex: true its convex polygons), or an error (for example for an element type that has no polygon).

triangles.description: The triangles covering the polygon of the element, holes excluded, as Archicad triangulates it.

vertices.description: The 2D coordinates of the three vertices of the triangle.

convexPolygons.description: With convex: true, the convex polygons the faces of the element's 3D model are decomposed into, body by body and face by face. Empty (or an error item instead) when the element has no solid 3D model of its own (the bodies of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, belong to their subelements, which can be given instead).

vertices.description: The 3D world coordinates of the vertices of the convex polygon, in order.

example.description: Triangulates the plan polygon of the first slabs with TriangulatePolygonsOfElements. Needs at least one Slab.
example.code:
"""Triangulates the plan polygon of the first slabs with TriangulatePolygonsOfElements.

Needs at least one Slab.
"""
import aclib

slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Slab'})['elements'][:3]
if not slabs:
    raise SystemExit ('No slab in the project.')

triangulations = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('TriangulatePolygonsOfElements', {'elements': slabs})['triangulations']
for slab, triangulation in zip (slabs, triangulations):
    print ('{}: {} triangles'.format (slab['elementId']['guid'], len (triangulation.get ('triangles', []))))

commands.name: GetTextureCoordinates
commands.description: Gets the texture coordinates (u, v) of the faces of the 3D model of the given elements: per solid body, per face, at the first vertex of the face. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

textureCoordinates.description: The texture coordinates of each element, aligned with the input: per solid body of its 3D model, or an error.

bodies.description: The solid bodies of the element's own 3D model, in Archicad's order, or an error for a body without texture information. Empty (or an error item instead) when the element has no solid 3D model of its own (the bodies of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, belong to their subelements, which can be given instead).

polygons.description: One item per face of the body, in Archicad's order: the texture coordinates at the first vertex of the face, or an error.

point.description: The first vertex of the face, in world coordinates.

u.description: The u texture coordinate at the point.

v.description: The v texture coordinate at the point.

commands.name: GetSurfaceTypesOfElements

The model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28.

surfaceTypes.description: The polygons of the 3D model of each element with their surface types, aligned with the input, or an error.

polygonIndex.description: The index of the polygon in the body, starting from 0.

polygonId.description: The identifier of the polygon in the 3D model (ModelerAPI::Polygon::GetPolygonId).

surfaceType.description: The surface type of the polygon: the numeric value of API_SurfaceTypeID as ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType returns it.

example.description: Reads the surface type of every polygon of a wall's 3D model with GetSurfaceTypesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:

commands.name: Get3DModelCounts
commands.description: Gets the number of components of each type (bodies, polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices, normal vectors, materials and lights) in the 3D model Archicad currently holds, as ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum counts them. A type that cannot be counted gets an error item. Available from Archicad 27.

counts.description: The number of components of each type in the 3D model Archicad currently holds, one item per type, or an error for a type that could not be counted.

componentType.description: The component type: the API_3DTypeID enumerator name without its API_ prefix and ID suffix.

count.description: The number of components of this type.

example.description: Prints how many bodies, polygons, edges, vertices etc. the current 3D model has, with Get3DModelCounts. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

commands.name: GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

elements.description: The elements to get the surface quantities of.

coverElements.description: Optional covering elements: the area where one of them overlaps a surface of an element is subtracted from that surface, so for example a slab on a wall takes its footprint off the top surface of the wall. When omitted, every Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Stair and Curtain Wall of the project is a covering element. Pass an empty array to get the whole surfaces with nothing subtracted. An element never covers itself.

surfaceQuantitiesOfElements.description: The surface quantities of the elements, in the order of the given elements. Areas are in square meters.

surfaces.description: The surfaces of the element as Archicad reports them: one item per surface attribute and building material pair of the element, so an element has as many items as it has distinct pairs (a basic wall with three different surfaces reports three items). Empty when Archicad reports no surface for the element, for example for an element without a 3D model.

surfaceId.description: The surface (material) attribute of the surface. Left out when the surface is not a project attribute, for example one defined by a GDL script.

buildingMaterialId.description: The building material of the part of the element the surface belongs to.

exposedArea.description: The area of the surface that is not covered by any of the covering elements, in square meters.

example.description: Reads the exposed surface areas of the first walls, with the slabs as covering elements, with GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements. Needs at least one Wall. Without coverElements every construction element covers the surfaces.

commands.name: GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements
commands.description: Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements. From Archicad 28 the subelements of external hierarchical elements (for example MEP elements or elements of other add-ons) are returned as externalSubelements.

items.description: Subelements grouped by type.

externalSubelements.description: The subelements of an external hierarchical element (for example an MEP element or an element of another add-on). Available from Archicad 28.

example.description: Lists the subelements (segments, frames, panels, treads, posts ...) of the curtain walls, stairs and railings with GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements. Needs at least one Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing.
example.code:
"""Lists the subelements (segments, frames, panels, treads, posts ...) of the curtain walls, stairs and railings with GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements.

Needs at least one Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing.
"""

elements = []
for elementType in ['CurtainWall', 'Stair', 'Railing']:
    elements += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': elementType})['elements']
if not elements:
    raise SystemExit ('No curtain wall, stair or railing in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements', {'elements': elements[:3]}))

commands.name: GetHierarchicalElementOwners
commands.description: Gets the owner of each given element in its hierarchical element: the root (e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing of a frame, tread or post) or the immediate parent. Also returns whether the given element is a main element, a subelement or not part of a hierarchical element.

elements.description: The elements whose owners are looked up, e.g. Curtain Wall frames or panels, Stair treads or Railing posts.

ownerMode.description: root (default): the root of the hierarchical element tree, e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing. parent: the immediate parent, which may itself be a subelement.

owners.description: The owner of each element, aligned with the input.

ownerElementId.description: The owner element. For a main element (e.g. a Curtain Wall) or an element that is not part of a hierarchical element, Archicad returns the input element itself.

hierarchicalElementType.description: The classification of the input element (not of its owner): MainElement is the main element of a hierarchical element (e.g. a Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing), ChildElement is a subelement of one (e.g. a frame or a tread), SingleElement is not part of a hierarchical element.

example.description: Finds the curtain wall each curtain wall frame belongs to with GetHierarchicalElementOwners. Needs at least one Curtain Wall.
example.code:
"""Finds the curtain wall each curtain wall frame belongs to with GetHierarchicalElementOwners.

Needs at least one Curtain Wall.
"""
import aclib

curtainWalls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'CurtainWall'})['elements'][:1]
if not curtainWalls:
    raise SystemExit ('No curtain wall in the project.')

subelements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements', {'elements': curtainWalls})['subelements']
frames = subelements[0].get ('cWallFrames', [])[:3]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHierarchicalElementOwners', {
    'elements': frames,
    'ownerMode': 'root'
}))

commands.name: EditHierarchicalElement
commands.description: Opens the given hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) in its hierarchical 3D editing mode, as the Edit button of the element does. Fails when Archicad is already in an editing mode. Leave the mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

elementId.description: The hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) to open in hierarchical editing mode.

example.description: Opens a curtain wall in its hierarchical editing mode with EditHierarchicalElement. While the mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command with error 4001 (ongoing user input), so the script cannot leave it: leave it yourself in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. Needs at least one Curtain Wall. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

While the mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command with error 4001 (ongoing user input),

commands.name: FinishHierarchicalEditing
commands.description: Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). The accept parameter is required, so changes are never discarded silently. Fails when Archicad is not in such an editing mode. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

accept.description: True to accept the changes made in the hierarchical editing mode (OK), false to discard them (Cancel).

example.description: Tries to leave a hierarchical editing mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing, discarding the changes (Cancel). accept True would keep the changes (OK). Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this call is refused then; leave the mode in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. When no editing mode is open, it fails with "not in a hierarchical editing mode". Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Tries to leave a hierarchical editing mode with FinishHierarchicalEditing, discarding the changes (Cancel).

accept True would keep the changes (OK). Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses
JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this call is refused then;
leave the mode in Archicad, with the button of the edit mode palette. When no editing mode is open,
it fails with "not in a hierarchical editing mode". Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FinishHierarchicalEditing', {'accept': False}))

commands.name: GetElementsInDrawOrder
commands.description: Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given.

elementType.description: Optional. Only elements of this type are returned, still in drawing order. If omitted, every element is returned.

filters.description: Optional. The filters an element must pass to be returned, the same as for GetElementsByType.

databases.description: The databases to list the elements of, each in its own drawing order. If omitted, the current database is used.

commands.name: GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements
commands.description: Returns the 2D drawing primitives (points, lines, arcs, texts, polylines, triangles, polygons, pictures) Archicad draws each given floor plan element from, in drawing order, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrimsExt decomposes it on every story and unclipped. Control items (type Ctrl_*) mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts such as hatches and texts. The floor plan must be the current database. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

drawingPrimitivesOfElements.description: The drawing primitives of each element, in the order of the input elements.

primitives.description: The primitives in the order Archicad draws them. The Ctrl_* items mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts (hatch borders, hatch lines, texts, curtain wall panels, ...).

type.description: The API_PrimTypeID name without its API_Prim prefix and ID suffix.

pen.description: The pen index of the primitive.

lineType.description: Line, Arc, PLine, Tri and Poly: the line type.

determination.description: How the type of the line or fill is determined (origin, inner line, contour line).

loc.description: Point: the location. Text: the left baseline position.

nArcs.description: The number of curved segments. Their geometry is not returned.

coordinates.description: PLine: the vertices. Tri: the three corners.

polygons.description: Poly: the sub polygons, the first one is the outline, the others are holes.

destBox.description: Pict: the bounding box of the picture.

hatchBorder.description: Ctrl_HatchBorderBeg and Ctrl_HatchLinesBeg: the fill that follows.

databaseId.description: A section, elevation or interior elevation database, for example as GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId returns it.

primitives.description: The primitives of the story levels drawn in the database, in the order Archicad draws them. The Ctrl_* items mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts (texts, ...).

type.description: The API_PrimTypeID name without its API_Prim prefix and ID suffix.

pen.description: The pen index of the primitive.

lineType.description: Line, Arc, PLine, Tri and Poly: the line type.

determination.description: How the type of the line or fill is determined (origin, inner line, contour line).

loc.description: Point: the location. Text: the left baseline position.

nArcs.description: The number of curved segments. Their geometry is not returned.

coordinates.description: PLine: the vertices. Tri: the three corners.

polygons.description: Poly: the sub polygons, the first one is the outline, the others are holes.

destBox.description: Pict: the bounding box of the picture.

hatchBorder.description: Ctrl_HatchBorderBeg and Ctrl_HatchLinesBeg: the fill that follows.

commands.name: GetSectionElements
commands.description: Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires.

databases.description: The section, elevation or interior elevation databases to list the section elements of. If omitted, the current database is used.

sectionElements.description: The elements drawn in the given databases, each with the owner element it was generated from.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of the section element itself, accepted by CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection as sectionElementId.

ownerElementId.description: The identifier of the owner element the section element was generated from - this is what every other listing command returns.

ownerElementType.description: The type of the owner element. Only present when the owner's header is readable from the section database.

example.description: Lists the elements drawn in the first section, each with the element it was generated from, with GetSectionElements. Needs at least one Section.

commands.name: GetRelationsOfElements

Available from Archicad 26.

otherElementType.description: Optional filter: only relations to elements of this type are returned.

relations.description: Type-specific relations of each element, aligned with the input.
