commands.name: LinkElements
commands.description: Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable.

links.description: The links to create, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

example.description: Links the first wall to the second one with LinkElements, reads the link back, then removes it. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way. Needs at least two Walls.

commands.name: UnlinkElements
commands.description: Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable.

links.description: The links to remove, each from one element to another.

executionResults.description: One result per link, aligned with the input.

example.description: Removes a link created by LinkElements with UnlinkElements. Links the first wall to the second one first, so it needs at least two Walls. Only the link in the given direction is removed.
example.code:
"""Removes a link created by LinkElements with UnlinkElements.

Links the first wall to the second one first, so it needs at least two Walls. Only the link in the given direction is removed.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:2]
if len (walls) < 2:
    raise SystemExit ('Fewer than two walls in the project.')
link = {'fromElementId': walls[0]['elementId'], 'toElementId': walls[1]['elementId']}

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('LinkElements', {'links': [link]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UnlinkElements', {'links': [{'fromElementId': walls[0]['elementId'], 'toElementId': walls[1]['elementId']}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetLinksOfElements', {'elements': walls[:1]})

commands.name: GetLinksOfElements
commands.description: Gets the links created by LinkElements that start from the given elements: the linked element and the flags of each link. Links pointing to an element are not returned; query the elements they start from. Returns an error item for an element that does not exist.

elements.description: The elements whose outgoing links are returned.

linksOfElements.description: The links starting from each element, aligned with the input.

commands.name: GetZoneBoundaries
commands.description: Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone.

zoneElementId.description: The identifier of a single Zone. Prefer the zones array: querying many Zones in one call is much faster than one call per Zone.

zones.description: A list of Zones. Only one of zoneElementId and zones can be given.

example.description: Reads the boundaries (bounding elements, neighbour zones ...) of the first zones with GetZoneBoundaries. Needs at least one Zone.

commands.name: GetZoneReductions
commands.description: Gets the area reductions of the given Zones, as the Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the polygons of the Zone covered by Walls, Columns, reducing Fills, sloping Roofs and low ceilings, each with its type, the percentage it is reduced by, its area and its outline with holes. Area calculations by local standards need these parts, which GetQuantitiesOfElements only gives as totals. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

elements.description: A list of Zones.

reductionsOfZones.description: The area reductions of each Zone, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

reductions.description: The reduction polygons of the Zone, as its Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the parts of the Zone polygon covered by Walls, Columns and reducing Fills, and the parts under a low ceiling (for example under a sloping Roof), each with the percentage it is reduced by and its area. Empty when nothing reduces the Zone's area.

type.description: What reduces the area in the polygon, as the DevKit's APIRoomReduction type of the polygon: Wall, Column, Hatch (a Fill set to reduce the Zone area), Gable (a low ceiling, for example the part under a sloping Roof below the low ceiling height), or Rest (the remaining polygon of the Zone). Unknown for a value this version of Tapir does not name.

percent.description: The percentage by which the area of the polygon reduces the Zone area, as the DevKit reports it.

area.description: The area of the polygon in square meters.

polygonOutline.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline of the polygon in meters; the last coordinate repeats the first.

polygonArcs.description: The arcs of the outline, indices into polygonOutline. Absent when the outline has no arc.

example.description: Reads the area reductions of the first zones (covered by walls, columns, fills or a low ceiling) with GetZoneReductions. Needs at least one Zone.
example.code:

commands.name: GetPropertyObjectsOfElements

The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

propertyObjectsOfElements.description: The property objects of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

propertyObjects.description: The property objects (library parts of the old listing system) of the element, linked to it by criteria or individually. Empty when the element has none.

libraryPartIndex.description: The index of the property object's library part, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

name.description: The name of the library part. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

guid.description: The guid of the library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

isIndividuallyAssigned.description: True when the property object is assigned to the element individually, false when it is linked by criteria.

commands.name: GetDescriptorsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the descriptors of the given elements: the listing descriptors in the property objects of each element, with the library part that declares them (index, name and guid), their listing database set and index, and their status (Normal, Deleted or Local). The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

descriptorsOfElements.description: The descriptors of each element, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

descriptors.description: The descriptors in the property objects of the element. Empty when the element has none.

libraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part that declares the descriptor, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

name.description: The name of the library part. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

guid.description: The guid of the library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

index.description: The index of the descriptor in the listing database set when status is Normal, in the library part when status is Local.

status.description: Normal: the descriptor exists in the listing database. Deleted: it is referenced, but deleted from the database. Local: it is defined in the library part. Unknown for a value this version of Tapir does not name.

commands.name: GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements
commands.description: Gets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, which of them match, and which one is assigned individually, each with the library part's index (the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts), name and guid. The output is aligned with the input array of elements.

elements.description: A list of elements, or of element types to read the links of the element defaults of that type.

elementType.description: Read the links of the element defaults of this type instead of an element.

linkedPropertyObjectsOfElements.description: The property object links of each element or element default, aligned with the input array of elements, or an error.

linkByCriteria.description: True when the property objects matching their criteria are linked to the element.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the individually assigned property object, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 when no property object is assigned individually.

individualLibraryPartName.description: The name of the individually assigned library part. Absent when there is none or it cannot be read.

individualLibraryPartGuid.description: The guid of the individually assigned library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when there is none or it cannot be read.

criteriaPropertyObjects.description: The linked property objects whose criteria match the element.

libraryPartIndex.description: The index of the property object's library part, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts.

name.description: The name of the library part. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

guid.description: The guid of the library part, the same as the guid returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. Absent when the library part cannot be read.

commands.name: SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements
commands.description: Sets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, and which one is assigned individually (0 removes the individual assignment). A link that is not given stays unchanged. All changes are made in one undoable step.

elementsWithLinkedPropertyObjects.description: The property object links to set, each for an element or for the element defaults of an element type. A link that is not given stays unchanged.

linkByCriteria.description: Link the property objects matching their criteria to the element.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the property object to assign to the element individually, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 removes the individually assigned property object.

elementType.description: Set the links of the element defaults of this type instead of an element.

linkByCriteria.description: Link the property objects matching their criteria to the element defaults.

individualLibraryPartIndex.description: The index of the library part of the property object to assign to the element defaults individually, the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts. 0 removes the individually assigned property object.

example.description: Switches the link by criteria of property objects on or off for a wall with SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Wall.

commands.name: UpdateZones
commands.description: Updates all Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements).

keepStampPosition.description: Keep the position of the Zone Stamps. The default is true.

undoTopTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the top of the Zones. The default is false.

undoBottomTrim.description: Undo the trimming of the bottom of the Zones. The default is false.

example.description: Updates the first zone of the project (geometry, Zone Stamp and connected elements) with UpdateZones. Changes the zone, as Design > Update Zones does. Archicad updates it right after the command has returned and clears the selection.
example.code:
"""Updates the first zone of the project (geometry, Zone Stamp and connected elements) with UpdateZones.

Changes the zone, as Design > Update Zones does. Archicad updates it right after the command has returned and clears the selection.
"""
import aclib

zones = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Zone'})['elements'][:1]
if not zones:
    raise SystemExit ('No zone in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UpdateZones', {
    'zones': zones,
    'keepStampPosition': True
}))

commands.name: SetZoneLabelingSettings
commands.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones on or off and selects the Label Favorite it places. Only the given settings are changed. Available from Archicad 28.

automaticLabeling.description: Turns the automatic labeling of Zones (placing a Label on each new Zone) on or off.

favoriteName.description: The name of the Label Favorite that is placed on each new Zone by the automatic labeling.

example.description: Switches the automatic labeling of zones on or off with SetZoneLabelingSettings, reads it back, then restores it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Switches the automatic labeling of zones on or off with SetZoneLabelingSettings, reads it back, then restores it.

Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

original = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetZoneLabelingSettings', {})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetZoneLabelingSettings', {'automaticLabeling': not original['isAutomaticLabelingOn']}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetZoneLabelingSettings', {})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetZoneLabelingSettings', {'automaticLabeling': original['isAutomaticLabelingOn']})

commands.name: GetZoneLabelingSettings
commands.description: Returns whether the automatic labeling of Zones is on and the name of the Label Favorite it places. Available from Archicad 28.

isAutomaticLabelingOn.description: Whether the automatic labeling of Zones (placing a Label on each new Zone) is on.

selectedFavoriteName.description: The name of the Label Favorite that is placed on each new Zone. Missing when no Favorite is selected.

example.description: Reads whether zones are labeled automatically and which Label Favorite is placed, with GetZoneLabelingSettings. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Reads whether zones are labeled automatically and which Label Favorite is placed, with GetZoneLabelingSettings.

Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetZoneLabelingSettings', {}))

commands.name: GetCollisions
commands.description: Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements.

volumeTolerance.description: Intersection body volume greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

performSurfaceCheck.description: Enables surface collision check. If disabled the surfaceTolerance value will be ignored. By default it's false.

surfaceTolerance.description: Intersection body surface area greater then this value will be considered as a collision. Default value is 0.001.

example.description: Finds the walls that collide with columns or beams with GetCollisions. Needs Walls and Columns or Beams.

commands.name: HighlightElements
commands.description: Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights. On Archicad 25 nonHighlightedColor is ignored.

highlightedColors.description: A list of colors to highlight elements.

items.description: Color of the highlighted element as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range.

wireframe3D.description: Optional parameter. Switch non highlighted elements in the 3D window to wireframe.

nonHighlightedColor.description: Optional parameter. Color of the non highlighted elements as an [r, g, b, a] array. Each component must be in the 0-255 range. Ignored on Archicad 25.

example.description: Highlights the walls in red, with the other elements in transparent blue and wireframe in 3D, with HighlightElements. Needs at least one Wall. The highlight is removed after 5 seconds.
example.code:
"""Highlights the walls in red, with the other elements in transparent blue and wireframe in 3D, with HighlightElements.

Needs at least one Wall. The highlight is removed after 5 seconds.
"""
import time
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('HighlightElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'highlightedColors': [[255, 0, 0, 255] for wall in walls],
    'wireframe3D': True,
    'nonHighlightedColor': [0, 0, 255, 128]
}))

time.sleep (5)

# An empty elements array removes the highlight.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('HighlightElements', {'elements': [], 'highlightedColors': []}))

commands.name: MoveElements
commands.description: Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

elementsWithMoveVectors.description: The elements with move vector pairs.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, then a copy of the element will be moved. By default it's false.

example.description: Moves a wall by 1 m along the X axis with MoveElements, then moves it back. Needs at least one editable Wall.

commands.name: RotateElements
commands.description: Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

beginPoint.description: Starting point of the rotation arc.

endPoint.description: End point of the rotation arc.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a copy of the element is rotated. By default it's false.

example.description: Rotates a wall by 90 degrees around the project origin with RotateElements, then rotates it back. Needs at least one editable Wall. The angle is the one between origin-beginPoint and origin-endPoint.

commands.name: MirrorElements
commands.description: Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently.

mirrorAxis.description: The mirror axis: the line through two points on the floor plan.

beginPoint.description: First point of the mirror axis.

endPoint.description: Second point of the mirror axis. Must differ from beginPoint.

copy.description: Optional parameter. If true, a mirrored copy of the element is created and the original is kept. By default it's false.

example.description: Mirrors a wall across the Y axis with MirrorElements, then mirrors it back. Needs at least one editable Wall. With copy True the original would be kept and a mirrored copy created.

commands.name: DeleteElements
commands.description: Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted.

elements.description: The elements to delete. The zones among them are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad.

example.description: Creates a wall and deletes it again with DeleteElements, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall and deletes it again with DeleteElements, first as a dry run that deletes nothing."""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls, 'dryRun': True}))
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: DeleteSelectedElements
commands.description: Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key.

example.description: Creates a wall, selects only it and deletes it with DeleteSelectedElements, the same as pressing the Delete key. The original selection is restored at the end. Run it with the floor plan open.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall, selects only it and deletes it with DeleteSelectedElements, the same as pressing the Delete key.

The original selection is restored at the end. Run it with the floor plan open.
"""
import aclib

originalSelection = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSelectedElements', {})['elements']
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeselectAll', {})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeSelectionOfElements', {'addElementsToSelection': walls})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteSelectedElements', {}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeSelectionOfElements', {'addElementsToSelection': originalSelection})

commands.name: LockElements
commands.description: Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

example.description: Locks a wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with LockElements, then unlocks it again. Needs at least one editable Wall.
example.code:
"""Locks a wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with LockElements, then unlocks it again.

Needs at least one editable Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')
wallId = walls[0]['elementId']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('LockElements', {'elements': walls}))
print ('Editable while locked: {}'.format (len (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FilterElements', {'elements': walls, 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements']) > 0))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UnlockElements', {'elements': walls})

commands.name: UnlockElements
commands.description: Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork!

example.description: Unlocks a locked wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with UnlockElements. Locks the first editable Wall first, so it is unchanged at the end.
example.code:
"""Unlocks a locked wall (manual lock, not Teamwork reservation) with UnlockElements.

Locks the first editable Wall first, so it is unchanged at the end.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall', 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable wall in the project.')
wallId = walls[0]['elementId']

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('LockElements', {'elements': walls})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('UnlockElements', {'elements': walls}))
print ('Editable after unlocking: {}'.format (len (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('FilterElements', {'elements': walls, 'filters': ['IsEditable']})['elements']) > 0))

commands.name: RefreshElements
commands.description: Refreshes (rebuilds) the given elements, for example placed Objects, Windows and Doors that still show the old geometry after their library part's script or embedded file changed. Set force to true to run the parameter script of GDL-based elements too. The elements are looked up in the current database (floor plan, section or detail window). Returns an execution result for each input element. The refresh cannot be undone.

force.description: Forces the rebuild of GDL-based elements, which runs their parameter script. The default is false.

example.description: Rebuilds the placed objects, windows and doors of the current database with RefreshElements. force True also runs their parameter script. The refresh cannot be undone.

commands.name: GetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements.

example.description: Lists the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of a placed object with GetGDLParametersOfElements. Needs at least one Object.
example.code:
"""Lists the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of a placed object with GetGDLParametersOfElements.

Needs at least one Object.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

parameters = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetGDLParametersOfElements', {'elements': objects})['gdlParametersOfElements'][0]['parameters']
for parameter in parameters:
    print ('{} ({}): {}'.format (parameter['name'], parameter['type'], parameter['value']))

commands.name: SetGDLParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution result naming it.

elementsWithGDLParameters.description: The elements with GDL parameters dictionary pairs.

example.description: Widens a placed object by 0.1 m through its GDL parameter A with SetGDLParametersOfElements, reads it back, then restores it. Needs at least one editable Object.

commands.name: GetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns.

markerParametersOfElements.description: The marker of each given element, in the order of the input, or an error for an element that is not a window or a door.

libPart.description: The library part of the marker. Absent when it could not be read.

parameters.description: The GDL parameters of the marker.

example.description: Reads the marker (the stamp next to the opening on the floor plan) library part and parameters of the first windows and doors with GetMarkerParametersOfElements. Needs at least one Window or Door.
example.code:
"""Reads the marker (the stamp next to the opening on the floor plan) library part and parameters of the first windows and doors with GetMarkerParametersOfElements.

Needs at least one Window or Door.
"""
import aclib

openings = []
for elementType in ['Window', 'Door']:
    openings += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': elementType})['elements']
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No window or door in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': openings[:3]}))

commands.name: SetMarkerParametersOfElements
commands.description: Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are.

elementsWithMarkerParameters.description: The elements with the marker parameters to change.

markerParameters.description: The marker parameters to change, each given by name or by index. The other marker parameters and the opening's own settings are left as they are.

name.description: The name of the marker parameter.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter: a number for the numeric types (Integer, Length, Angle, RealNumber, PenColor, LineType, Material, FillPattern, BuildingMaterial, Profile, RGBColor, Intensity), a string for String and Title, true/false for Boolean and 'On'/'Off' for LightSwitch. Array parameters are not supported.

index.description: The index of the marker parameter, as GetMarkerParametersOfElements reports it.

value.description: The new value of the marker parameter, see the value given with a name.

example.description: Changes one marker parameter of a window or door with SetMarkerParametersOfElements, then restores it. Needs at least one Window or Door whose marker has a String parameter.
example.code:
"""Changes one marker parameter of a window or door with SetMarkerParametersOfElements, then restores it.

Needs at least one Window or Door whose marker has a String parameter.
"""
import aclib

openings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Window'})['elements']
openings += aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Door'})['elements']
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No window or door in the project.')

opening = openings[0]
marker = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': [opening]})['markerParametersOfElements'][0]
stringParameters = [p for p in marker.get ('parameters', []) if p['type'] == 'String' and 'value' in p and 'dimension1' not in p]
if not stringParameters:
    raise SystemExit ('The marker of the first opening has no String parameter.')

parameter = stringParameters[0]
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elementsWithMarkerParameters': [{
    'elementId': opening['elementId'],
    'markerParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': 'Tapir'}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elements': [opening]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetMarkerParametersOfElements', {'elementsWithMarkerParameters': [{
    'elementId': opening['elementId'],
    'markerParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': parameter['value']}]
}]}))

commands.name: GetURLReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Gets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA.

urlReferences.description: The web link of each given element, or an error. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA.

oneOf.title: URLReference
oneOf.description: The web link of an element.

url.description: The URL of the link, e.g. https://www.graphisoft.com.

description.description: The description of the link, e.g. GRAPHISOFT Home Page.

example.description: Prints the web link (URL and description) of every wall with GetURLReferencesOfElements. Walls without a link get an APIERR_NOUSERDATA error item.
example.code:
"""Prints the web link (URL and description) of every wall with GetURLReferencesOfElements.

Walls without a link get an APIERR_NOUSERDATA error item.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: SetURLReferencesOfElements
commands.description: Sets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. Fails with APIERR_MOREUSER for an element that already holds a link.

elementsWithURLReferences.description: The elements and the web link to set on each.

url.description: The URL of the link, e.g. https://www.graphisoft.com. At most 511 bytes in UTF-8.

description.description: The description of the link, e.g. GRAPHISOFT Home Page. At most 255 bytes in UTF-8. Empty when omitted.

example.description: Gives the first wall without a web link a link with SetURLReferencesOfElements and reads it back. Needs a Wall without a link. The link stays on the wall: this command cannot replace or remove an existing link.
example.code:
"""Gives the first wall without a web link a link with SetURLReferencesOfElements and reads it back.

Needs a Wall without a link. The link stays on the wall: this command cannot replace or remove an
existing link.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

links = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elements': walls})['urlReferences']
wallsWithoutLink = [wall for wall, link in zip (walls, links) if 'error' in link]
if not wallsWithoutLink:
    raise SystemExit ('Every wall has a link already.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elementsWithURLReferences': [{
    'elementId': wallsWithoutLink[0]['elementId'],
    'url': 'https://www.graphisoft.com',
    'description': 'GRAPHISOFT Home Page'
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetURLReferencesOfElements', {'elements': wallsWithoutLink[:1]})

commands.name: ChangeLibraryPartOfElements
commands.description: Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type, given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B).

elementsWithLibraryPart.description: The elements with the library part to change them to. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects.

libraryPart.description: The new library part, given by one of name, index or guid. It has to be a placeable library part of the element's type in the loaded libraries.

name.description: The name of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it in documentName.

index.description: The index of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it.

guid.description: The main guid of the library part, as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it in guid.

keepParameters.description: Copies the values of the element's GDL parameters to the parameters of the new library part that have the same name, type and array dimensions; the other parameters get the new part's defaults. Default: true.

keepSize.description: Keeps the size (A and B) of the element; when false, the element gets the new part's default size. Default: true.

example.description: Sets the first object to the library part it already uses with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Giving the part it already has leaves the project unchanged; give the name of another library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it.
example.code:
"""Sets the first object to the library part it already uses with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements.

Needs at least one Object. Giving the part it already has leaves the project unchanged; give the name
of another library part (see GetAvailableLibraryParts) to replace it.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

details = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': objects})['detailsOfElements'][0]
libraryPartName = details['details']['libPart']['name']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeLibraryPartOfElements', {'elementsWithLibraryPart': [{
    'elementId': objects[0]['elementId'],
    'libraryPart': {'name': libraryPartName},
    'keepParameters': True,
    'keepSize': True
}]}))

commands.name: GetHotspotsOfElements
commands.description: Gets the 2D hotspots of the given library part instances (Objects, Lamps, Windows, Doors, Skylights, Zones, Curtain Wall parts, etc.), e.g. to dimension to them.

hotspotsOfElements.description: The hotspots of the given library part instances, in the order of the input.

hotspots.description: The 2D hotspots of the placed library part instance, as Archicad returns them.

example.description: Prints the 2D hotspots of the first object with GetHotspotsOfElements. Needs at least one Object.
example.code:
"""Prints the 2D hotspots of the first object with GetHotspotsOfElements.

Needs at least one Object.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements'][:1]
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetHotspotsOfElements', {'elements': objects}))

commands.name: RunParameterScriptOfElements
commands.description: Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements.

example.description: Runs the parameter script of every object with RunParameterScriptOfElements. Needs at least one Object. Parameters that depend on other parameters are recalculated.
example.code:
"""Runs the parameter script of every object with RunParameterScriptOfElements.

Needs at least one Object. Parameters that depend on other parameters are recalculated.
"""
import aclib

objects = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Object'})['elements']
if not objects:
    raise SystemExit ('No object in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RunParameterScriptOfElements', {'elements': objects}))

commands.name: CreateColumns
commands.description: Creates Column elements based on the given parameters.

columnsData.description: Array of data to create Columns.

items.description: The parameters of the new Column.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

height.description: Optional column height.

axisRotationAngle.description: Optional column rotation angle in radians.

slantAngle.description: Optional slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also makes the column slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

slantDirectionAngle.description: Optional rotation angle of the slanted column on the horizontal plane in radians.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments. Only effective for rectangular columns.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

example.description: Creates two columns with CreateColumns: one with the Column tool defaults and one round, 3 m high column. Coordinates are in meters; z is the elevation of the column base.

commands.name: CreateWalls
commands.description: Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Wall favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (structure, reference line location, top link, offsets, ...) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. With a favorite only begCoordinate and endCoordinate are needed.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

floorIndex.description: Story index (as returned by GetStories). When provided, zCoordinate is interpreted as bottomOffset relative to the floor. Takes priority over zCoordinate for floor assignment.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z when floorIndex is absent; bottomOffset relative to the floor when floorIndex is provided.

height.description: Optional explicit height. Sets relativeTopStory to 0, so it replaces the top link of the favorite or the tool default. When omitted, the height and top link of the favorite (or of the Wall tool defaults) are kept.

thickness.description: Optional thickness. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's thickness is kept. Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Without structureType the new wall keeps the structure of the favorite (or the wall tool default), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

offset.description: Optional reference line offset. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's offset is kept.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero creates a curved wall (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

referenceLineLocation.description: Optional. When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's reference line location is kept. The Core* values only have an effect on a Composite or Profile wall.

flipped.description: Optional. True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped). When omitted, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's side is kept, which for a Profile wall mirrors its whole cross section.

structureType.description: Optional. When neither this nor one of the attribute ids below is given, the favorite's or the Wall tool default's structure is kept.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

linkToSettings.description: When newCreationMode is true, homeStoryDifference overrides the home story selected by floorIndex or derived from zCoordinate.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

example.description: Creates a straight and a curved wall with CreateWalls. Fields not given (structure, top link, ...) come from the Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
example.code:
"""Creates a straight and a curved wall with CreateWalls.

Fields not given (structure, top link, ...) come from the Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.
"""
import aclib
import math

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {
        'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0},
        'height': 3.0,
        'thickness': 0.3
    },
    {
        'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0},
        'endCoordinate': {'x': 8.0, 'y': 4.0},
        'arcAngle': math.pi / 4,
        'height': 3.0
    }
]}))

commands.name: CreateBeams

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index to place the new element on. It must be an existing, unlocked layer. When omitted the element gets the layer of the favorite or of the tool defaults.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

slantAngle.description: Slant angle in radians. A non-zero value also switches the beam to slanted, unless isSlanted is given explicitly.

isSlanted.description: Optional explicit slanted state. By default it is derived from slantAngle.

profileAngle.description: Rotation angle of the profile around the beam's center line, in radians.

arcAngle.description: Optional arc angle in radians. A non-zero value makes a horizontally curved beam.

verticalCurveHeight.description: Optional rise of a vertically curved beam. A non-zero value makes a vertically curved beam; it wins over arcAngle.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored if profileId is also given. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true (the default), Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

commands.name: SolveStairBaseline
commands.description: Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27.

stairsData.description: Array of Stair data to check, with the same fields as the items of CreateStairs (without favoriteName). Nothing is created.

items.description: The parameters of the Stair to check. Fields that are not given come from the current Stair tool defaults, as in CreateStairs.

baseLinePoints.description: 2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline. Minimum 2 points for a straight stair, 3+ for L-shaped or U-shaped stairs.

zCoordinate.description: The Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the stair base.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from zCoordinate.

finishVisible.description: Optional. If false, the tread/riser finishes are hidden and only the stair structure (e.g. a monolith) is modeled.

solutions.description: The results of the stair solver, aligned with the input stairsData.

solution.description: Correct: the baseline was already valid, nothing changed. Solved: the solver turned it into a valid baseline, returned in baseLinePoints. NotSolved: no valid baseline was found; CreateStairs is likely to fail or create an invalid stair with this input.

baseLinePoints.description: The baseline polyline after the solver ran.

baseLineArcs.description: The arcs of the baseline after the solver ran, indexing baseLinePoints. Present only when the baseline has arcs.

totalHeight.description: Total height of the stair after the solver ran.

flightWidth.description: Width of the stair flight after the solver ran.

stepNum.description: Number of risers after the solver ran.

riserHeight.description: Height of each riser after the solver ran.

treadDepth.description: Depth (going) of each tread after the solver ran.

example.description: Checks an L-shaped stair baseline with SolveStairBaseline, without creating a stair. Prints whether the baseline is Correct, Solved (with the solved baseline) or NotSolved. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

"""

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SolveStairBaseline', {'stairsData': [{
    'baseLinePoints': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 3.0}, {'x': 3.0, 'y': 3.0}],

    'totalHeight': 3.0,
    'flightWidth': 1.2
}]}))

name.description: The name of the parameter.

value.description: The value of the parameter as the parameter list holds it: a number, a boolean, a string, or 'On' or 'Off' for a LightSwitch. For an array parameter, a list of its dimension1 x dimension2 items, the first index outer.

commands.name: SetOpeningSymbolParameters
commands.description: Changes the GDL parameters of the cut and uncut floor plan symbols of Opening elements, in the format of SetGDLParametersOfElements. Only the given parameters are changed. Available from Archicad 29.

cutSymbolParameters.description: The GDL parameters to change, by name, in the format SetGDLParametersOfElements uses. The parameters left out are not changed.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

index1.description: The 1-based first index of the one item of an array parameter to change. Only with a single value.

index2.description: The 1-based second index of the item to change, only together with index1. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The new value, in the format the parameter list was read in. For an array parameter without index1, a list of all of its items, flat (the first index outer) or as a list of rows; resizing an array is not supported.

unCutSymbolParameters.description: The GDL parameters to change, by name, in the format SetGDLParametersOfElements uses. The parameters left out are not changed.

name.description: The name of the parameter.

index1.description: The 1-based first index of the one item of an array parameter to change. Only with a single value.

index2.description: The 1-based second index of the item to change, only together with index1. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The new value, in the format the parameter list was read in. For an array parameter without index1, a list of all of its items, flat (the first index outer) or as a list of rows; resizing an array is not supported.

example.description: Flips a Boolean parameter of the cut symbol of the first opening with SetOpeningSymbolParameters, then restores it. Needs an Opening (made with the Opening tool) with a cut symbol that has a Boolean parameter. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Flips a Boolean parameter of the cut symbol of the first opening with SetOpeningSymbolParameters, then restores it.

Needs an Opening (made with the Opening tool) with a cut symbol that has a Boolean parameter.
Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

openings = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Opening'})['elements'][:1]
if not openings:
    raise SystemExit ('No opening in the project.')

symbol = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': openings})['openings'][0]
booleans = [p for p in symbol.get ('cutSymbolParameters', []) if p['type'] == 'Boolean' and 'dimension1' not in p]
if not booleans:
    raise SystemExit ('The first opening has no cut symbol with a Boolean parameter.')

parameter = booleans[0]
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'cutSymbolParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': not parameter['value']}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': openings})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetOpeningSymbolParameters', {'elements': [{
    'elementId': openings[0]['elementId'],
    'cutSymbolParameters': [{'name': parameter['name'], 'value': parameter['value']}]
}]}))

commands.name: SetOpeningDetails
commands.description: Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29.

openingsWithDetails.description: The Opening elements (made with the Opening tool) to change, each with the details to set. A detail that is left out stays as it is.

parentElementId.description: The new element the opening belongs to.

addCutElements.description: Elements the opening should cut as well.

removeCutElements.description: Elements the opening should no longer cut.

polygon.description: The new polygon of the opening, in the plane of the xAxis and yAxis returned by GetOpeningDetails.

transformation.description: A transformation applied to the opening's geometry: a 3x4 matrix of 12 numbers, row by row, the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers being the translation along X, Y and Z. For example [1,0,0,1, 0,1,0,0, 0,0,1,0] moves the opening by 1 along X.

anchor.description: The anchor point of the opening's polygon.

extrusionSurfaceId.description: The surface of the extrusion faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

endSurfaceId.description: The surface of the end faces. Only used when the surface is overridden.

example.code:
"""Moves the first opening 0.5 m along X with SetOpeningDetails, reads it back, then moves it back.

Needs at least one Opening (made with the Opening tool). The transformation is a 3x4 matrix, row by
row, with the translation in the 4th, 8th and 12th numbers. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

commands.name: CreateMorphs
commands.description: Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions.

size.description: Builds a simple axis-aligned box of this size. Mutually exclusive with `body` - give exactly one of the two.

body.description: Builds arbitrary geometry instead of a simple box. Mutually exclusive with `size` - give exactly one of the two.

topExpansion.description: Only used with `size` (box) morphs. Expands the top rectangle outwards on all four sides by this amount, creating a frustum (e.g. sloped excavation shape). 0 creates a cuboid.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the basePoint's z value.

example.description: Creates a 2 m box morph and a tetrahedron morph from vertices and faces with CreateMorphs. A body's vertices are local to the morph's basePoint; each face lists vertex indices counterclockwise as seen from outside. An item may also name a Morph favorite to start from (favoriteName), a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id), as the box does with its id.

commands.name: CreateRoofs
commands.description: Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from level.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Without structureType the new roof keeps the structure of the roof tool default (or the favorite), which may be a composite; send structureType 'Basic' for the thickness to apply.

pivotLine.description: If given, creates a single-plane roof instead of a multi-plane roof, tilted along this pivot line.

angle.description: Slope angle of the single-plane roof in radians. Only valid together with 'pivotLine'.

example.description: Creates a multi-plane roof and a single-plane roof with CreateRoofs. A pivotLine makes a single-plane roof that rises on the left of the line; angles are in radians.

commands.name: CreateRailings
commands.description: Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices.

railingsData.description: Array of data to create Railings.

items.description: The parameters of the new Railing. Everything not given here - the posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters - comes from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults of the open project. Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices from them.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the railing on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index (home story) of the railing. The story is made active in the floor plan while the railing is created and the previously active story is restored afterwards. When omitted, the current story.

bottomOffset.description: Optional base height of the railing relative to the floor level. When omitted, the value of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

height.description: Optional height of the railing segments. When omitted, the segment height of the favorite (or of the Railing tool defaults) is kept.

example.description: Creates a 1.1 m high railing along three edges of a balcony with CreateRailings. The posts, rails, handrails and infill come from the Railing tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

commands.name: CreateCurtainWalls
commands.description: Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid.

curtainWallsData.description: Array of data to create Curtain Walls.

items.description: The parameters of the new Curtain Wall. Everything not given here - the frame and panel classes, the surfaces, the boundary and corner frames, the pattern - comes from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults of the open project.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates becomes one straight segment, so two coordinates give a single-segment curtain wall.

zCoordinate.description: Optional Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. When omitted, the base level of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) relative to the floor is kept.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. When omitted, derived from zCoordinate if that is given, otherwise the current story.

height.description: Optional height of the curtain wall. When omitted, the height of the favorite (or of the Curtain Wall tool defaults) is kept.

primaryPattern.description: Optional column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segment (the primary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

secondaryPattern.description: Optional row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). When omitted, the pattern of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) is kept.

cells.description: Optional assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. A cell not listed here keeps the assignment of the favorite (or of the tool defaults) when the pattern is unchanged, otherwise the assignment of the first default cell.

example.description: Creates a 6 m long, 3 m high curtain wall with 1.5 m wide columns and two rows with CreateCurtainWalls. The frame and panel classes come from the Curtain Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

The frame and panel classes come from the Curtain Wall tool defaults, or from favoriteName.

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateCurtainWalls', {'curtainWallsData': [{

    'zCoordinate': 0.0,
    'height': 3.0,
    'primaryPattern': {'sizes': [1.5], 'logic': 'FixedSizes'},
    'secondaryPattern': {'sizes': [1.0, 2.0], 'logic': 'FixedSizes'}
}]}))

commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensions
commands.description: Creates associative linear dimensions from explicit witness point references. A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight and textPen for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

example.description: Creates a wall and dimensions its length with CreateAssociativeDimensions. The dimension follows the wall: inIndex 1 and 2 are the end points of the wall's reference line. A witness point given only by a coordinate is static. direction is the direction of the dimension line.

commands.name: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection
commands.description: Creates associative linear dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column and opening presets. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Dimension favorite to base the new dimension on, e.g. for its layer, line pen and markers. Its settings are applied first, then the command sets the geometry and its usual text placement. The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight and textPen for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

sectionElementId.description: The identifier of a single section element. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

sectionElementIds.description: A list of section elements whose preset points are merged into one continuous dimension chain. Only one of sectionElementId and sectionElementIds can be given.

example.description: Dimensions the composite faces of the first wall in the current section with CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection. Run it with a section window as the current window that shows at least one Wall. The dimension is placed in that section.
example.code:
"""Dimensions the composite faces of the first wall in the current section with CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection.

Run it with a section window as the current window that shows at least one Wall. The dimension is
placed in that section.
"""
import aclib

sectionElements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSectionElements', {})['sectionElements']
walls = [s for s in sectionElements if s.get ('ownerElementType') == 'Wall']
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the current section window.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection', {'dimensionsData': [{
    'sectionElementId': walls[0]['sectionElementId'],
    'referencePoint': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'preset': 'WallCompositeFaces'
}]}))

The favorite's text size, text pen and text frame are not applied (tested in Archicad 28): use textHeight and textPen for the texts. The Dimension tool defaults are left as they were.

textHeight.description: Optional height of the dimension texts in millimeters (paper size), applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

textPen.description: Optional pen index of the dimension texts, applied to every witness point after favoriteName.

commands.name: GetDimensionData
commands.description: Gets witness point data (coordinates, measured values) from existing dimension chains.

Needs at least one Dimension. The witness point fields are the ones CreateAssociativeDimensions takes,

commands.name: GetOpeningTransformations
commands.description: Gets the placement of Opening elements, Windows, Doors and Skylights without changing them: a global-to-local transformation matrix, its inverse, and the origin and axes in world coordinates derived from the inverse. For Windows, Doors and Skylights the local-to-global matrix is the one Archicad returns, and mirrored ones give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). For Opening elements it is built from the opening geometry (Archicad 29 and later): origin at the anchor point, the X and Y axes of the opening and Z = X × Y, which points against the extrusion direction. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

openingTransformations.description: The transformation of each given Opening, or an error, in the order of the input elements.

globalToLocal.description: The global-to-local matrix (API_Tranmat), the inverse of localToGlobal: the 12 values of a 3x4 matrix, row by row, so x' = m[0]*x + m[1]*y + m[2]*z + m[3], y' = m[4]*x + ... + m[7], z' = m[8]*x + ... + m[11].

localToGlobal.description: The local-to-global matrix, in the same layout: the matrix ACAPI_Element_GetOpeningTransformation returns for a Window, Door or Skylight, or the one built from the geometry of an Opening element.

origin.description: The origin of the opening's local coordinate system in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. For an Opening element this is its anchor point.

xAxis.description: The local X axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal.

yAxis.description: The local Y axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal.

zAxis.description: The local Z axis in world coordinates, from localToGlobal. For an Opening element it is X × Y, which points against its extrusion direction.

determinant.description: The determinant of the 3x3 part of localToGlobal: 1, or -1 for a mirrored Window, Door or Skylight.

isMirrored.description: True when the matrix is left-handed (negative determinant), which Archicad returns for a mirrored opening.

example.description: Prints the placement (transformation matrices, origin and axes) of every window with GetOpeningTransformations. Needs at least one Window; Doors, Skylights and Openings work the same way (Openings from Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the placement (transformation matrices, origin and axes) of every window with GetOpeningTransformations.

Needs at least one Window; Doors, Skylights and Openings work the same way (Openings from Archicad 29).
Requires Archicad 27 or later.
"""
import aclib

windows = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Window'})['elements']
if not windows:
    raise SystemExit ('No window in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetOpeningTransformations', {'elements': windows}))

commands.name: CreateZones
commands.description: Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters.

zonesData.description: Array of data to create Zones.

items.description: The parameters of the new Zone.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorIndex.description: Optional story index of the new zone. An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) is found around its reference point on this story, which is made active in the floor plan while the zone is created; the previously active story is restored afterwards.

name.description: Name of the zone.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

stampAngle.description: Optional zone stamp rotation angle in radians.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

contourLine.description: Optional contour line of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.

coverFill.description: Optional cover fill of the zone. Fields that are left out keep the value of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults.

height.description: Optional height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height); when omitted, the height and top link of the favorite or of the Zone tool defaults are kept. Do not combine with relativeTopStory.

bottomOffset.description: Optional base level of the zone relative to its home story level.

topOffset.description: Optional offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Optional top link: non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not combine with height.

floorThickness.description: Optional thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

example.description: Creates a 6 m x 5 m zone named Office from its outline with CreateZones. A zone that would overlap an existing zone on the same story fails with an error instead (unless allowOverlap is true). Give 'geometry': {'referencePosition': {'x': ..., 'y': ...}} instead to create an automatic zone in the room around that point.

commands.name: CreatePolylines
commands.description: Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters.

polylinesData.description: Array of data to create Polylines.

items.description: The parameters of the new Polyline.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the polyline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

linePenIndex.description: Pen index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, by default the current pen is used.

lineTypeIndex.description: Line type attribute index of the polyline contour. Optional parameter, by default the current line type is used.

penWeightMm.description: Optional pen weight override in mm.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.

example.description: Creates a polyline of two straight segments and one arc segment with CreatePolylines. arcAngle is in radians; arcs refer to the indices of the coordinates.
example.code:
"""Creates a polyline of two straight segments and one arc segment with CreatePolylines.

arcAngle is in radians; arcs refer to the indices of the coordinates.
"""
import aclib
import math

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreatePolylines', {'polylinesData': [{
    'coordinates': [
        {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
        {'x': 3.0, 'y': 3.0},
        {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0},
        {'x': 9.0, 'y': 0.0}
    ],
    'arcs': [{'begIndex': 2, 'endIndex': 3, 'arcAngle': math.pi / 2}]
}]}))

commands.name: CreateHatches
commands.description: Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters. A hatch can have holes, in the same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts for hatches.

hatchesData.description: Array of data to create Hatches.

items.description: The parameters of the new Hatch.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the hatch on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the hatch outline. Do not repeat the first point at the end.

arcs.description: The arcs of the hatch outline.

holes.description: Optional holes of the hatch, each with its polygonOutline and optional polygonArcs (arc indices are relative to the hole's own outline). The same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts and GetDetailsOfElements returns for hatches.

contourPenIndex.description: Optional pen index for the contour. By default the current pen is used.

fillPenIndex.description: Optional pen index for the fill. By default the current pen is used.

foregroundColor.description: Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill foreground, used instead of fillPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillPenIndex when both are given. The same format as the colors returned by GetZoneCategories and GetPenTables.

backgroundColor.description: Optional RGB color (components between 0.0 and 1.0) of the fill background, used instead of fillBackgroundPenIndex. Takes precedence over fillBackgroundPenIndex when both are given.

fillId.description: Optional fill attribute. By default the current fill is used.

roomSpecial.description: Special area percent in a room (negative means OFF).

example.description: Creates a 4 m x 4 m hatch with a 1 m x 1 m hole and a red foreground with CreateHatches. Don't repeat the first point at the end of the outline. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the spline on. Optional parameter, by default the current layer is used.

closed.description: Is this a closed curve? Optional, defaults to false.

roomSeparator.description: Is this a zone boundary line? Optional, defaults to false.
