commands.name: CreateObjects
commands.description: Creates Object elements based on the given parameters.

objectsData.description: Array of data to create Objects.

items.description: The parameters of the new Object.

libraryPartName.description: The name of the library part to use.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

example.description: Places the first Object library part of the loaded libraries at the origin with CreateObjects. Give any loaded library part name in libraryPartName, e.g. one listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.
example.code:
"""Places the first Object library part of the loaded libraries at the origin with CreateObjects.

Give any loaded library part name in libraryPartName, e.g. one listed by GetAvailableLibraryParts.
"""
import aclib

libraryParts = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAvailableLibraryParts', {'filterByTypeId': 'Object'})['libraryParts']
if not libraryParts:
    raise SystemExit ('No Object library part in the loaded libraries.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateObjects', {'objectsData': [{
    'libraryPartName': libraryParts[0]['documentName'],
    'coordinates': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0},
    'angle': 0.0
}]}))

commands.name: GetGridElementDefaults
commands.description: Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

elementId.description: The grid element. The zero GUID for the tool defaults.

variation.description: Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.

floorIndex.description: Home story index.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index.

pos.description: Insertion point: the start of the grid line.

angle.description: Direction of the grid line in radians.

length.description: Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.

xRatio.description: The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.

yRatio.description: The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.

useXYFixSize.description: Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.

level.description: Elevation of the object from its home story.

libraryPartName.description: Localized name of the library part.

parameters.description: GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.

type.description: Integer, Length, Angle, RealNum, LightSwitch, ColorRGB, Intensity, LineType, Material, FillPattern, PenColor, String, Boolean, Title, BuildingMaterial, Profile, Dictionary or Unknown.

value.description: Number for numeric and boolean types, string for String and Title. Not given for arrays.

dimension1.description: First dimension of an array parameter.

dimension2.description: Second dimension of an array parameter.

example.description: Prints the library part, size and GDL parameters a new grid element gets from the Grid Tool defaults, with GetGridElementDefaults. Requires Archicad 26 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the library part, size and GDL parameters a new grid element gets from the Grid Tool defaults, with GetGridElementDefaults.

Requires Archicad 26 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetGridElementDefaults', {}))

elementId.description: The grid element. The zero GUID for the tool defaults.

variation.description: Four-character variation of the object: 'GREL' for a grid element.

floorIndex.description: Home story index.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index.

pos.description: Insertion point: the start of the grid line.

angle.description: Direction of the grid line in radians.

length.description: Length of the grid line: the GDL parameter AC_Length of the Grid Tool's grid marker, or the object's A size for a library part without it.

xRatio.description: The object's xRatio as stored: its A size with useXYFixSize on, otherwise the A size divided by the library part's own A.

yRatio.description: The object's yRatio as stored, like xRatio for the B size.

useXYFixSize.description: Whether xRatio and yRatio hold the sizes themselves.

level.description: Elevation of the object from its home story.

libraryPartName.description: Localized name of the library part.

parameters.description: GDL parameters, separators left out. Only when requested.

type.description: Integer, Length, Angle, RealNum, LightSwitch, ColorRGB, Intensity, LineType, Material, FillPattern, PenColor, String, Boolean, Title, BuildingMaterial, Profile, Dictionary or Unknown.

value.description: Number for numeric and boolean types, string for String and Title. Not given for arrays.

dimension1.description: First dimension of an array parameter.

dimension2.description: Second dimension of an array parameter.

example.description: Prints the position, direction, length and library part of every grid element with GetGridElements. Set includeParameters to True to get their GDL parameters as well. Requires Archicad 26 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the position, direction, length and library part of every grid element with GetGridElements.

Set includeParameters to True to get their GDL parameters as well. Requires Archicad 26 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetGridElements', {'includeParameters': False}))

commands.name: CreateGridElements
commands.description: Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later.

begCoordinate.description: Start point of the grid line (the object's insertion point).

endCoordinate.description: End point of the grid line. Sets the direction and, unless lengthMode is 'none', the length.

lengthMode.description: How the line length is applied. length (default): to the GDL parameter AC_Length when the library part has it, as the Grid Tool's grid marker does; otherwise to the object's A size, converted to xRatio as CreateObjects does. none: the length is left to 'parameters'.

floorIndex.description: Home story index. Default: the tool default.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index. Only a positive index takes effect. Default: the tool default.

parameters.description: GDL parameters to set by name (read the names with GetGridElementDefaults). The value is a number, a boolean or a string. Unknown names and wrong value types are reported in warnings and skipped. The tool defaults can look different from a grid drawn with the Grid Tool (for example a short line with a leader to the bubble); to get the same look, copy the parameters of such a grid (GetGridElements with includeParameters).

value.description: A number or a boolean for a numeric parameter, a string for a String or Title parameter.

warnings.description: Parameters that were not set, prefixed with the index of the grid element.

example.description: Creates two crossing 20 m long grid lines with CreateGridElements. The library part comes from the Grid Tool defaults; parameters sets GDL parameters by name (see GetGridElementDefaults). Requires Archicad 26 or later.

commands.name: CreateLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements based on the given parameters.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create Labels.

items.description: The parameters of the new Label.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

parentElementId.description: The parent element if the label is an associative label.

labelClass.description: Optional; if omitted, inherits the current Label tool default (which may silently resolve to either class - explicitly setting this avoids ambiguity). 'Symbol' needs a symbol library part, which only the Label tool default or the favorite given in favoriteName can provide: when those are a Text label, the item fails instead of placing a label without content.

text.description: The text content if the label is a text label. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

runs.description: Multi-style text content for a text label: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

begCoordinate.description: The begin coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter, but either begCoordinate or parentElementId must be provided. Unless midCoordinate and endCoordinate are both given too, the label is created at its default position relative to the parent element (Archicad's 'createAtDefaultPosition'), so the label may not end up at begCoordinate - read it back with GetDetailsOfElements after creation.

midCoordinate.description: The mid coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with endCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

endCoordinate.description: The end coordinate of leader line. Optional parameter; give it together with midCoordinate to place the label exactly where the coordinates say.

floorInd.description: The identifier of the floor. Optional parameter, by default the current floor or the floor of the parent element is used.

example.description: Labels the first wall with a text label with CreateLabels. Needs at least one Wall. Without parentElementId the label stands on its own at begCoordinate.
example.code:
"""Labels the first wall with a text label with CreateLabels.

Needs at least one Wall. Without parentElementId the label stands on its own at begCoordinate.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLabels', {'labelsData': [{
    'parentElementId': walls[0]['elementId'],
    'labelClass': 'Text',
    'text': 'Exterior wall'
}]}))

commands.name: CreateTexts
commands.description: Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

textsData.description: Array of data to create Texts.

items.description: The parameters of the new Text element.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a favorite to base the new element on. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

coordinate.description: The placement position of the text. The z value is used to determine the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

text.description: The text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF. Ignored if 'runs' is also given.

runs.description: Multi-style text content: an array of styled runs, concatenated in order. Takes precedence over 'text' if both are given.

height.description: The character height in millimeters. Optional; defaults to the Text tool default. Equivalent to style.height.

pen.description: Optional pen attribute index. Equivalent to style.penIndex.

angle.description: Optional rotation angle in radians. Equivalent to style.angle.

style.description: height/pen/angle/justification above take precedence over the same fields here if both are given.

floorIndex.description: Optional floor index. If omitted, derived from the coordinate's z value.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index. If omitted, the Text tool default layer is used.

example.description: Creates a plain text and a two-line text with a bold first line with CreateTexts. height is the character height in millimeters (paper size).

commands.name: CreateLevelDimensions
commands.description: Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes.

levelDimensionsData.description: Array of data to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan).

items.description: The parameters of the new Level Dimension.

favoriteName.description: Optional name of a Level Dimension favorite to base the new element on. Its settings (marker, format, text style, layer, pen) are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them.

id.description: Optional Element ID of the new element (the ID field of the Settings dialog, shown in schedules and labels; the same string GetDetailsOfElements returns as id). When omitted the element gets the next automatic ID of its tool.

position.description: The location of the marker on the floor plan. With a parentElementId it must lie on that element, the measured level is the parent's height at this point. Outside the parent's outline Archicad still creates the dimension, but without a height (GetDetailsOfElements reads a level of -110000000).

parentElementId.description: Optional element the level dimension is associated with (Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Beam, Column, Wall, Object, Stair ...). The dimension then shows the element's height at the position and follows the element when it changes. Without it the dimension measures the floor level, or the given static level.

level.description: Optional fixed level value in meters (absolute, from the project zero). Only used without parentElementId; the dimension then shows this value instead of the floor level.

floorIndex.description: The index of the floor to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the floor of the parent element, otherwise the current floor is used.

layerIndex.description: Layer attribute index to place the dimension on. Optional parameter, by default the layer of the favorite or the Level Dimension tool default is used.

pen.description: Pen index of the marker. Optional parameter.

textHeight.description: Height of the dimension text in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

textPen.description: Pen index of the dimension text. Optional parameter.

dimForm.description: Marker type of the Level Dimension tool, 0-19 as Archicad stores it (read it back with GetDetailsOfElements from an existing level dimension or one placed with a favorite). Optional parameter.

needPlus.description: Show a plus sign for positive values. Optional parameter.

markerSize.description: Size of the marker in millimeters (paper size). Optional parameter.

angle.description: Rotation angle of the marker in radians. Optional parameter.

origin.description: The origin the level is measured from. Optional parameter.

example.description: Creates a slab and puts an associative level dimension on it with CreateLevelDimensions, plus one showing a fixed level. The associative one shows the slab's level at its position and follows the slab when it changes; level (in meters, from the project zero) is only used without parentElementId.

commands.name: ModifyWalls
commands.description: Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters.

geometryType.description: Polygonal is not settable here; it is read-only via GetDetailsOfElements. This is unrelated to slantAlpha/slantBeta - see profileType for the cross section shape those depend on.

arcAngle.description: Arc angle in radians; non-zero makes the wall curved (begCoordinate/endCoordinate are the chord endpoints).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - whichever is applied last wins, and Archicad recomputes the actual height from the story elevations once relativeTopStory is non-zero.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) wall - a Composite or Profile wall takes its thickness from the composite or profile attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch such a wall first.

flipped.description: True mirrors the wall to its reference line (the side GetDetailsOfElements reports as flipped).

profileType.description: slantAlpha/slantBeta only have an effect once this is set to Slanted.

slantAlpha.description: Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.

slantBeta.description: Only has an effect once profileType is set to Slanted or Trapez.

topOffset.description: Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the wall's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

visibility.description: Confirmed live on Archicad 29 (#852): a wall there knows only 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories' (Wall Settings offers no Custom option), and Archicad silently drops every other combination written here although the command reports success - showAllAbove, showAllBelow, showRelAbove and showRelBelow (any value, 0 included) and showOnHome true -> false all read back unchanged. 'All relevant stories' is isAutoOnStoryVisibility true. 'Home story only' takes two calls: first isAutoOnStoryVisibility true (Archicad resets the custom fields to 0), then isAutoOnStoryVisibility false with visibility { showOnHome: true }. Archicad 30 adds a Custom option for walls; whether the other fields become writable there is untested.

isAutoOnStoryVisibility.description: When true (the default on a new wall), Archicad recomputes 'visibility' automatically from the wall's vertical extent and ignores any value set for it. Setting 'visibility' without also setting this field turns it off automatically. See the note on 'visibility' for which combinations a wall accepts.

contourPen.description: Pen of the wall's own contour/reference outline (API_WallType::contPen) - distinct from cutFillPen, which is the cut fill pattern's pen. Not inheritable/overridable like cutFillPen, it is the wall's own pen index directly, the same field regardless of structureType.

contourPen3D.description: Pen of the wall's contour in 3D views (API_WallType::contPen3D).

contourLineTypeId.description: Line type of the wall's own contour (API_WallType::contLtype) - pairs with contourPen, which only sets the pen, not the line type.

belowViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "OutLines Only" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup (API_WallType::belowViewLineType).

aboveViewLinePen.description: Pen used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup.

aboveViewLineTypeId.description: Line type used when "Overhead All" is selected from the "Floor Plan Display" popup - pairs with aboveViewLinePen.

viewDepthLimitation.description: Only has an effect on a multi-story wall (relativeTopStory/topOffset making it span more than one story).

useCompositePriority.description: When true, the Composite's own priority is used at junctions instead of connectionPriority.

inheritEndSurface.description: The end surface of the wall is inherited from the adjoining wall.

alignTexture.description: Align texture mapping to the wall's edges.

polyCanChange.description: The polygonal wall's corners can be changed in case of L and T connections. Only meaningful for a Polygonal wall (geometryType).

materialsChained.description: Whether the surface materials are chained.

logHeight.description: Height of the log for log walls. 0 means a normal (non-log) wall.

example.description: Creates a wall, then makes it longer, higher and thicker with ModifyWalls. Only the given fields change. A new thickness only takes effect on a Basic wall.
example.code:
"""Creates a wall, then makes it longer, higher and thicker with ModifyWalls.

Only the given fields change. A new thickness only takes effect on a Basic wall.
"""
import aclib

wall = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'height': 3.0
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyWalls', {'wallsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': wall['elementId'],
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'height': 3.5,
    'structureType': 'Basic',
    'thickness': 0.4
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [wall], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyBeams
commands.description: Modifies Beam elements based on the given parameters.

width.description: Cross section width of the beam. Applied to all segments.

height.description: Cross section height of the beam. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and height equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/height independent values. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round beam cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the beam to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

holes.description: Replaces all holes currently placed on the beam.

example.description: Creates a beam, then changes its cross section and adds a round hole with ModifyBeams. Only the given fields change; holes replaces every hole of the beam.
example.code:
"""Creates a beam, then changes its cross section and adds a round hole with ModifyBeams.

Only the given fields change; holes replaces every hole of the beam.
"""
import aclib

beam = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateBeams', {'beamsData': [{
    'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'endCoordinate': {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0},
    'zCoordinate': 3.0
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyBeams', {'beamsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': beam['elementId'],
    'isWidthAndHeightLinked': False,
    'width': 0.3,
    'height': 0.6,
    'holes': [{'type': 'Circular', 'centerX': 3.0, 'centerZ': 0.3, 'width': 0.15}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [beam], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifySlabs
commands.description: Modifies Slab elements based on the given parameters.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the slab's reference level. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative level.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) slab - a Composite slab takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite slab first.

polygonOutline.description: Replaces the slab's entire polygon, including its holes - resend the holes field too to keep them, otherwise they are removed.

holes.description: Can be given on its own, without polygonOutline, to add/remove/clear holes in place (an empty array clears all holes) - the slab's current outline is reused unchanged.

example.description: Creates a slab, then raises it, makes it thicker and replaces its outline with ModifySlabs. Only the given fields change; polygonOutline replaces the whole polygon, holes included.
example.code:
"""Creates a slab, then raises it, makes it thicker and replaces its outline with ModifySlabs.

Only the given fields change; polygonOutline replaces the whole polygon, holes included.
"""
import aclib

slab = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateSlabs', {'slabsData': [{
    'level': 0.0,
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 4.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0}]
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifySlabs', {'slabsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': slab['elementId'],
    'zCoordinate': 0.5,
    'structureType': 'Basic',
    'thickness': 0.3,
    'polygonOutline': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 6.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 4.0}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [slab], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyColumns
commands.description: Modifies Column elements based on the given parameters.

zCoordinate.description: Absolute Z of the column's bottom. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given; a Z below the lowest story stays on the lowest story with a negative bottomOffset.

floorIndex.description: Optional home story index (as returned by GetStories). With zCoordinate it pins the story the Z is resolved against; alone it only changes the home story (combine with bottomOffset to set the offset relative to it).

height.description: Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height). Do not combine with relativeTopStory in the same call - see the note on relativeTopStory below.

isFlipped.description: Has no visible effect on a circular column (circleBased cross section) - Archicad ignores it there.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the column's top to another story instead of an explicit height - do not set together with 'height' in the same call, see the note on 'height' above.

width.description: Cross section width of the column. Applied to all segments.

depth.description: Cross section depth (height) of the column. Applied to all segments.

isWidthAndHeightLinked.description: When true, Archicad keeps width and depth equal and setting one changes the other - set to false first to give width/depth independent values. Applied to all segments.

circleBased.description: True for a round column cross section, false for rectangular. Ignored once profileId switches the column to a custom profile shape. Applied to all segments.

buildingMaterialId.description: Cross section building material (round or rectangular, per circleBased). Applied to all segments.

profileId.description: Switches the cross section to this custom extruded profile (circleBased becomes false). Applied to all segments.

example.description: Creates a column, then moves it, rotates it by 45 degrees and makes it 0.5 m x 0.3 m with ModifyColumns. Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
example.code:
"""Creates a column, then moves it, rotates it by 45 degrees and makes it 0.5 m x 0.3 m with ModifyColumns.

Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
"""
import aclib
import math

column = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateColumns', {'columnsData': [{
    'coordinates': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0}
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyColumns', {'columnsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': column['elementId'],
    'origin': {'x': 2.0, 'y': 1.0},
    'axisRotationAngle': math.radians (45),
    'circleBased': False,
    'isWidthAndHeightLinked': False,
    'width': 0.5,
    'depth': 0.3
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': [column], 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyWindows
commands.description: Modifies Window elements based on the given parameters.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

example.description: Creates a wall with a window, then makes the window wider and moves it along the wall with ModifyWindows. Only the given fields change. centerOffset is measured along the wall from its begin point.

commands.name: ModifyDoors
commands.description: Modifies Door elements based on the given parameters.

reveal.description: Turn the reveal on or off.

revealDepthOffset.description: Distance the frame plane is moved across the wall thickness, along the wall normal.

example.description: Creates a wall with a door, then mirrors the door and moves it along the wall with ModifyDoors. Only the given fields change. centerOffset is measured along the wall from its begin point.

commands.name: ModifyMorphs
commands.description: Modifies Morph elements based on the given parameters.

rotationDegreesZ.description: Turns the Morph about the vertical axis through its origin, counterclockwise seen from above, in degrees. Added to the current rotation.

body.description: When given, discards the Morph's ENTIRE existing geometry and rebuilds it from this (mirrors CreateProfiles' replaceSkins) - not a partial edit.

xAxis.description: Replaces the rotation part of the placement transform outright. Give all three of xAxis/yAxis/zAxis together. If rotationDegreesZ is also given in the same call, it is applied first and this then overwrites its result.

example.description: Creates a box morph, then moves it 3 m along X and turns it by 30 degrees with ModifyMorphs. rotationDegreesZ is in degrees and is added to the current rotation.

commands.name: ModifyRoofs
commands.description: Modifies multi-plane Roof elements based on the given parameters.

thickness.description: Only takes effect on a Basic (homogeneous) roof - a Composite roof takes its thickness from the composite attribute. Send structureType 'Basic' in the same call to switch a composite roof first.

example.description: Creates a multi-plane and a single-plane roof, then changes both with ModifyRoofs. The multi-plane roof is raised and gets a new slope and eaves overhang. The single-plane roof gets a steeper angle, a new pivot line and a wider outline. Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
example.code:
"""Creates a multi-plane and a single-plane roof, then changes both with ModifyRoofs.

The multi-plane roof is raised and gets a new slope and eaves overhang. The single-plane roof gets a
steeper angle, a new pivot line and a wider outline. Only the given fields change. Angles are in radians.
"""
import aclib
import math

roofs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRoofs', {'roofsData': [{
    'level': 3.0,
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 8.0, 'y': 6.0}, {'x': 0.0, 'y': 6.0}],
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (30)}]
}, {
    'level': 3.0,
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 12.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': 0.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': 4.0}, {'x': 12.0, 'y': 4.0}],
    'pivotLine': {'begCoordinate': {'x': 12.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 18.0, 'y': 0.0}},
    'angle': math.radians (15)
}]})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyRoofs', {'roofsWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': roofs[0]['elementId'],
    'level': 3.5,
    'eavesOverhang': 0.5,
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (40)}]
}, {
    'elementId': roofs[1]['elementId'],
    'angle': math.radians (25),
    'pivotLine': {'begCoordinate': {'x': 12.0, 'y': -1.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 18.0, 'y': -1.0}},
    'polygonOutline': [{'x': 12.0, 'y': -1.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': -1.0}, {'x': 18.0, 'y': 5.0}, {'x': 12.0, 'y': 5.0}]
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': roofs, 'fields': ['details']})

commands.name: ModifyShells
commands.description: Modifies the structure (Basic or Composite, building material or composite) of Shell elements based on the given parameters.

example.description: Makes the first shell a Basic shell of the first building material with ModifyShells, reads it back, then restores its structure. Needs at least one Shell.

commands.name: ModifyMeshes
commands.description: Modifies the attributes of Mesh elements based on the given parameters.

example.description: Creates a flat mesh, then gives it a skirt and a raised corner with ModifyMeshes. Only the fields given in meshData change; polygonCoordinates replaces the whole outline, z being the height of each point above level.

commands.name: ModifyObjects
commands.description: Modifies Object elements based on the given parameters.

objectsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

example.description: Places an object, then moves it, turns it by 90 degrees and mirrors it with ModifyObjects. The object is the first Object library part of the loaded libraries. Angles are in radians.

commands.name: ModifyLamps
commands.description: Modifies Lamp elements based on the given parameters.

lampsWithDetails.description: Array of elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

fixPoint.description: 0-based index of the hotspot to keep fixed (raw API_ObjectType.fixPoint value, not 1-based).

offset.description: Offset of the symbol's origin from the insertion point. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default hotspot offset regardless of what is sent) - same class of read-only-in-practice field as Morph's bodyType/edgeType/level.

useFixedAngle.description: Use a fixed rotation angle. Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify.

lightColor.description: Reported accurately on Get, but confirmed live that Archicad silently discards this value through both Create and Modify (Get always reports the library part's own default light color). lightIsOn (the on/off state, as opposed to the color) does not have this problem.

example.description: Places a lamp, then raises it, switches it off and makes its light blue with ModifyLamps. The lamp is the first Lamp library part of the loaded libraries. Colors are RGB values between 0 and 1.

commands.name: ModifyTexts
commands.description: Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters.

textsWithDetails.description: Array of Text elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the element auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run text applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

coordinate.description: The new placement position. As in CreateTexts, the z value selects the floor when floorIndex is omitted.

floorIndex.description: Optional. Moves the text to this floor; when omitted and a coordinate is given, the floor is derived from its z value.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

example.description: Creates a text, then replaces its content, makes it bold and 5 mm high, and moves it with ModifyTexts. Only the given fields change; text replaces the whole content (see ChangeTextContent to change a part).

commands.name: ModifyLabels
commands.description: Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters.

labelsWithDetails.description: Array of Label elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. The label's class (Text/Symbol) cannot be changed after creation. A change of the text, the runs, or a run-level style field (pen, font, faces, height, effects) rebuilds the content as one paragraph, which makes the label's text auto-width (word wrap off), as SetDetailsOfElements does, and on a multi-run label applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the content as it is.

text.description: The new text content. Newlines create multiple lines; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are normalized to LF.

example.description: Creates a wall with a text label, then changes the label's text, frame and arrow with ModifyLabels. Only the given fields change.

commands.name: ModifyCurtainWalls
commands.description: Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls.

curtainWallsWithDetails.description: Array of Curtain Wall elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the others, and the frames and panels not affected by them, are left as they are. The fields are those of CreateCurtainWalls, so a curtain wall can be changed in place instead of being deleted and recreated, keeping its GUID, properties and classifications.

coordinates.description: The new 2D coordinates of the reference line of the curtain wall on the floor plan. Each pair of consecutive coordinates is one straight segment, so the number of coordinates must be the current number of segments plus one: the segments can be moved and resized, but not added or removed (a curved segment becomes straight).

zCoordinate.description: The new Z coordinate (absolute elevation) of the bottom of the curtain wall. The home story is derived from it unless floorIndex is given too.

floorIndex.description: The new home story index. On its own it moves the curtain wall to that story, keeping its bottom offset from the story; with zCoordinate it pins the story the bottom elevation is measured from.

height.description: The new height of the curtain wall.

primaryPattern.description: The new column pattern: the sizes of the columns along the segments (the primary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.

secondaryPattern.description: The new row pattern: the sizes of the rows from the bottom up (the secondary grid). Applied to every segment of the curtain wall; the frames and panels are regenerated from it.

cells.description: Assignment of panel and frame classes to the cells of the pattern unit of every segment, as in CreateCurtainWalls. Without a pattern change, a cell not listed here keeps its current assignment; with one, it takes the assignment of the first current cell.

example.description: Creates a curtain wall, then makes it 4 m high with 1 m wide columns with ModifyCurtainWalls. The curtain wall keeps its GUID, properties and classifications.

commands.name: ChangeTextContent
commands.description: Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content.

contentChanges.description: The content changes, applied in order (several changes of one element see the content as the previous one left it). Unlike ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels, the rest of the content is not rebuilt: the other runs, their styles and any autotext in them stay as they are, and the inserted piece takes the style of the character at 'from'.

elementId.description: A Text element or a Label of the Text class.

from.description: The position in the content where the replaced range starts.

range.description: The number of characters to replace; 0 inserts the content at 'from'. The range may not reach over a line end into another paragraph.

content.description: The new content of the range; an empty string deletes the range. It must not contain line ends.

example.description: Creates the text 'Hello World', then replaces 'World' with 'Tapir' with ChangeTextContent. from is the character position, range the number of characters replaced (0 inserts). The styles of the rest of the content and the autotexts in it are kept. A range must stay within one line.
example.code:
"""Creates the text 'Hello World', then replaces 'World' with 'Tapir' with ChangeTextContent.

from is the character position, range the number of characters replaced (0 inserts). The styles of
the rest of the content and the autotexts in it are kept. A range must stay within one line.
"""
import aclib

text = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateTexts', {'textsData': [{
    'coordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0},
    'text': 'Hello World'
}]})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ChangeTextContent', {'contentChanges': [{
    'elementId': text['elementId'],
    'from': len ('Hello '),
    'range': len ('World'),
    'content': 'Tapir'
}]}))

commands.name: ModifyZones
commands.description: Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, height, base offset, top link and floor thickness. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon is kept.

zonesWithDetails.description: Array of Zone elements to modify, with the fields to change. Only the given fields are changed; the polygon and the omitted fields are kept. The same fields as the ZoneSettings of SetDetailsOfElements.

name.description: Name of the zone.

categoryAttributeId.description: The identifier of the zone category attribute.

stampPosition.description: Position of the origin of the zone stamp.

stampAngle.description: Rotation angle of the zone stamp in radians.

fixedStampAngle.description: If true, the zone stamp angle remains fixed when the element is rotated.

height.description: Height of the zone from its bottom. Sets relativeTopStory to 0 (explicit height), so do not combine it with relativeTopStory in the same call: whichever is applied last wins.

bottomOffset.description: Base level of the zone relative to its home story level.

topOffset.description: Offset of the top of the zone from the linked top story level. Only has an effect when relativeTopStory is non-zero.

relativeTopStory.description: Non-zero links the top of the zone to another story, relative to its home story (1 is the story above), instead of an explicit height. Do not set together with height in the same call, see the note on height.

floorThickness.description: Thickness of the floor finish (subfloor thickness) of the zone.

example.description: Renames and renumbers the first zone with ModifyZones, reads it back, then restores its name and number. Needs at least one Zone. Only the given fields change; the polygon is kept.
example.code:
"""Renames and renumbers the first zone with ModifyZones, reads it back, then restores its name and number.

Needs at least one Zone. Only the given fields change; the polygon is kept.
"""
import aclib

zones = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Zone'})['elements'][:1]
if not zones:
    raise SystemExit ('No zone in the project.')

old = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': zones, 'fields': ['details']})['detailsOfElements'][0]['details']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyZones', {'zonesWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': zones[0]['elementId'],
    'name': 'Meeting Room',
    'numberStr': 'M01'
}]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetDetailsOfElements', {'elements': zones, 'fields': ['details']})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ModifyZones', {'zonesWithDetails': [{
    'elementId': zones[0]['elementId'],
    'name': old['name'],
    'numberStr': old['numberStr']
}]}))

commands.name: MeasureTexts
commands.description: Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing.

texts.description: The texts to measure, each with the font, style and height it would be placed with. Nothing is created.

text.description: The text to measure. Newlines separate lines, each measured on its own; Windows-style CRLF (and bare CR) line endings are treated as LF.

fontIndex.description: The index of the font, as GetDetailsOfElements and GetFontsByName report it in fontIndex. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

fontName.description: Name of the font as Archicad's font list carries it (GetDetailsOfElements reports it in fontName), which is not always the operating system's font name; GetFontsByName tells whether a name is found. Resolved to the font's index (exact match first, then case-insensitive); the text fails when no loaded font has the name. Takes precedence over fontIndex if both are given. One of fontName and fontIndex is required.

height.description: The character height in millimetres, as a Text's height.

slant.description: The slant angle of the characters in radians; pi/2 (the default) is upright text.

inModelUnits.description: When true, Archicad applies the drawing scale correction and the lengths are model distances at the current drawing scale; when false (the default), they are lengths on paper in millimetres.

measurements.description: One item per input text, in the same order. The measurement takes no width factor or character spacing into account.

length.description: The length of the longest line.

longestLineIndex.description: The zero-based index of the longest line (the first of them on a tie).

lineLengths.description: The length of every line, in order. An empty line is 0.

capitalSizeFactor.description: The ratio of the font's capital size to its typographic size. Absent when Archicad does not return it for the font.

example.description: Measures the length of each line of a two-line text in Arial 2.5 mm, on paper and in the model, with MeasureTexts. Creates nothing. Model lengths use the drawing scale of the current window.
example.code:
"""Measures the length of each line of a two-line text in Arial 2.5 mm, on paper and in the model, with MeasureTexts.

Creates nothing. Model lengths use the drawing scale of the current window.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MeasureTexts', {'texts': [
    {'text': 'Living Room\n24.5 m2', 'fontName': 'Arial', 'height': 2.5},
    {'text': 'Living Room\n24.5 m2', 'fontName': 'Arial', 'height': 2.5, 'bold': True, 'inModelUnits': True}
]}))

commands.name: GetElementPreviewImage
commands.description: Returns the preview image of the given element.

imageType.description: The type of the preview image. Default is 3D.

format.description: The image format. Default is png.

width.description: The width of the preview image in pixels. Default is 128.

height.description: The height of the preview image in pixels. Default is 128.

commands.name: SetElementNotificationClient
commands.description: Sets up a new notification client to receive element events.

host.description: The host address of the notification client. If not provided, localhost is used.

port.description: The port number of the notification client.

notifyOnNewElement.description: Notify on creation of a new element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnModificationOfAnElement.description: Notify on modification/deletion of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.

notifyOnReservationChanges.description: Notify on reservation changes of an element. Optional parameter, by default true.

example.description: Prints the element events Archicad sends to a local HTTP server registered with SetElementNotificationClient. Creates a column to trigger a notification, then removes the client again. Archicad posts each event as JSON to http://<host>:<port>/element_notification. Modifications are observed only for columns here (elementTypesToObserve): attaching an observer to every element blocks Archicad for minutes on a project with thousands of elements.
example.code:
"""Prints the element events Archicad sends to a local HTTP server registered with SetElementNotificationClient.

Creates a column to trigger a notification, then removes the client again. Archicad posts each event
as JSON to http://<host>:<port>/element_notification.

Modifications are observed only for columns here (elementTypesToObserve): attaching an observer to
every element blocks Archicad for minutes on a project with thousands of elements.
"""
import aclib
import json
import threading
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

HOST = 'localhost'
PORT = 12345

class NotificationHandler (BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST (self):
        length = self.headers.get ('Content-Length')
        body = self.rfile.read (int (length)) if length else self.rfile.readline ()
        print (json.dumps (json.loads (body), indent = 4))
        self.send_response (200)
        self.end_headers ()

server = HTTPServer ((HOST, PORT), NotificationHandler)
threading.Thread (target = server.serve_forever, daemon = True).start ()

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetElementNotificationClient', {
    'host': HOST,
    'port': PORT,
    'notifyOnNewElement': True,
    'notifyOnModificationOfAnElement': True,
    'elementTypesToObserve': ['Column'],
    'notifyOnReservationChanges': False
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateColumns', {'columnsData': [{'coordinates': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0, 'z': 0.0}}]})
time.sleep (2)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RemoveElementNotificationClient', {'host': HOST, 'port': PORT})
server.shutdown ()

commands.name: RegularizePolygons
commands.description: Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project.

polygons.description: The polygons to regularize, in the format of CreateSlabs (polygonCoordinates, polygonArcs, holes). For CreateHatches, pass the outline of a result as its coordinates and arcs.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline. A last coordinate equal to the first is ignored.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every vertex and edge of the results which input vertex or edge it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polygon, in the order of the request.

polygons.description: The valid polygons Archicad made of the input: none, one or more.

polygonCoordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the outline, without a closing coordinate.

ancestry.description: Only with withAncestry. Read from the vertexAncestry and edgeAncestry of Archicad's API_RegularizedPoly; -1 marks a vertex or edge that Archicad created (for example at a self-intersection).

contours.description: One item per contour of this result: the outline first, then the holes in order.

vertices.description: For each vertex of the contour, the input vertex it came from.

items.description: An input vertex or edge: the contour (0 is the outline, k the hole at index k-1 of the request) and the vertex or edge in it (edge i runs from vertex i to the next one). Both are -1 when Archicad created it.

edges.description: For each edge of the contour (edge i runs from vertex i to the next one), the input edge it came from.

items.description: An input vertex or edge: the contour (0 is the outline, k the hole at index k-1 of the request) and the vertex or edge in it (edge i runs from vertex i to the next one). Both are -1 when Archicad created it.

example.description: Regularizes a self-intersecting (bow tie) outline with a repeated point with RegularizePolygons. The results are in the format of CreateSlabs; nothing is created.

commands.name: RegularizePolylines

The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project.

polylines.description: The polylines to regularize, in the format of CreatePolylines.

withAncestry.description: Also return for every point and segment of the results which input point or segment it came from. Optional, false by default.

results.description: One item per input polyline, in the order of the request.

coordinates.description: The 2D coordinates of the regularized polyline. Empty when nothing valid is left of it.

arcs.description: The arcs of the regularized polyline.

ancestry.description: Only with withAncestry. Read from the vertexAncestry and edgeAncestry of Archicad's API_RegularizedPoly; -1 marks a vertex or edge that Archicad created (for example at a self-intersection).

vertices.description: For each point of the result, the index of the input point it came from.

items.description: An input point or segment by its index (segment i runs from point i to point i+1); -1 when Archicad created it.

edges.description: For each segment of the result (segment i runs from point i to point i+1), the index of the input segment it came from.

items.description: An input point or segment by its index (segment i runs from point i to point i+1); -1 when Archicad created it.

example.description: Removes the repeated points of a polyline with RegularizePolylines, and reports which input point each result point came from. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines; nothing is created.

commands.name: ImportFavorites
commands.description: Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project. From Archicad 29 they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or the given fileNames) or from a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format), with the conflict policies Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting and RenameNew.

path.description: Absolute path on the AC host. With the prefs format: a Favorites file (.prefs) or folder. With the xml format: the folder of Favorite files, as ExportFavorites writes it. With the legacyPRF format: the .prf file.

format.description: The format to import from, the counterpart of the format of ExportFavorites. prefs (the default) works in every Archicad version. xml imports Favorite files from a folder, and legacyPRF a Favorites file of earlier Archicad versions; these two require Archicad 29 or newer.

fileNames.description: Only with the xml format: the names of the Favorite files in the folder to import. Default: every Favorite file of the folder.

targetFolder.description: Folder hierarchy under which to import. Empty = root. With the xml and legacyPRF formats the folder must exist, and omitting it keeps the folders stored with the Favorites.

importFolders.description: Only with the prefs format: if true and `path` is a folder, the folder structure is preserved.

conflictPolicy.description: How to resolve name conflicts. The prefs format takes Error, Skip, Overwrite or Append, default Overwrite. The xml and legacyPRF formats take Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting or RenameNew, default Error.

firstConflictName.description: Set when conflictPolicy=Error and a name collided; absent otherwise.

example.description: Imports a Favorite from a .prefs file with ImportFavorites. Needs at least one Wall. The script creates the Favorite 'Tapir Example Wall' from the first wall, exports it to a temporary file, deletes it, imports it again from the file and finally deletes it.
example.code:
"""Imports a Favorite from a .prefs file with ImportFavorites.

Needs at least one Wall. The script creates the Favorite 'Tapir Example Wall' from the first wall, exports it to a
temporary file, deletes it, imports it again from the file and finally deletes it.
"""
import os
import tempfile

import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

favoriteName = 'Tapir Example Wall'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateFavoritesFromElements', {
    'favoritesFromElements': [{'elementId': walls[0]['elementId'], 'favorite': favoriteName}]
})

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory () as tempDir:
    favoritesFile = os.path.join (tempDir, 'TapirExample.prefs')
    aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ExportFavorites', {'path': favoritesFile, 'names': [favoriteName]})
    aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteFavorites', {'favorites': [favoriteName]})

    aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportFavorites', {
        'path': favoritesFile,
        'format': 'prefs',
        'conflictPolicy': 'Skip'
    }))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetFavoritesByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteFavorites', {'favorites': [favoriteName]})

commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements
commands.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes.

items.description: The identifier of the element and the name of the Favorite to apply to it.

applySettings.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc.). Geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is never applied - the element stays on its own home story - except that a Window or Door takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included, while keeping its wall, marker and placement. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. A Dimension's text size, text pen and text frame are not changed (tested in Archicad 28): the dimension creation commands take textHeight and textPen for them. Default is true.

applyClassifications.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's classifications. Default is true.

applyCategories.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.

applyProperties.description: Whether to apply the Favorite's property values. Default is true.

keepFields.description: Fields of the target element to keep: after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width', 'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column; 'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height', 'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a story. Default: nothing is kept.

example.description: Applies the first Wall Favorite to a new wall with ApplyFavoritesToElements, keeping the wall's height. Needs a Wall Favorite. The wall is created by the script and deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Applies the first Wall Favorite to a new wall with ApplyFavoritesToElements, keeping the wall's height.

Needs a Wall Favorite. The wall is created by the script and deleted at the end.
"""
import aclib

wallFavorites = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetFavoritesByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['favorites']
if not wallFavorites:
    raise SystemExit ('The project has no Wall Favorite.')

wall = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {
    'wallsData': [{'begCoordinate': {'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 5.0, 'y': 0.0}, 'height': 3.0}]
})['elements'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ApplyFavoritesToElements', {
    'favoritesToApply': [{'elementId': wall['elementId'], 'favorite': wallFavorites[0]}],
    'applySettings': True,
    'applyClassifications': True,
    'applyCategories': True,
    'applyProperties': False,
    'keepFields': ['height', 'topOffset', 'relativeTopStory']
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': [wall]})

commands.name: GetPropertyValuesOfElements
commands.description: Returns the property values of the elements for the given property. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With includeAvailability it also tells whether each property is available for the element.

commands.name: AddPropertyToAttributes
commands.description: Makes an existing custom property available for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only.

example.code:
"""Makes a custom property available for the first Building Material with AddPropertyToAttributes, then removes it again.

Needs a custom property that the Building Material does not have yet. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.
"""
import aclib

buildingMaterial = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes'][0]
attributeIds = [{'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']}]
ownPropertyIds = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds})['propertyDefinitionsOfAttributes'][0].get ('propertyIds', [])
customProperties = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['properties']
propertyId = next ((p['propertyId'] for p in customProperties if {'propertyId': p['propertyId']} not in ownPropertyIds), None)
if propertyId is None:
    raise SystemExit ('No custom property that the Building Material does not have.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddPropertyToAttributes', {'propertyId': propertyId, 'attributeIds': attributeIds}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds, 'properties': [{'propertyId': propertyId}]})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RemovePropertyFromAttributes', {'propertyId': propertyId, 'attributeIds': attributeIds})

"""Makes a custom property unavailable for the first Building Material with RemovePropertyFromAttributes.

The script first makes a property available that the Building Material does not have yet, so the project
ends as it was. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.
"""
import aclib

buildingMaterial = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes'][0]
attributeIds = [{'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']}]
ownPropertyIds = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds})['propertyDefinitionsOfAttributes'][0].get ('propertyIds', [])
customProperties = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['properties']
propertyId = next ((p['propertyId'] for p in customProperties if {'propertyId': p['propertyId']} not in ownPropertyIds), None)
if propertyId is None:
    raise SystemExit ('No custom property that the Building Material does not have.')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes', {'attributeIds': attributeIds, 'properties': [{'propertyId': propertyId}]})

commands.name: ImportPropertiesXml
commands.description: Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed.

xml.description: A Property Manager export (XML) to import.

example.description: Imports a group with one text property from Property Manager XML with ImportPropertiesXml, then deletes them. conflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a property whose name already exists in its group.
example.code:
"""Imports a group with one text property from Property Manager XML with ImportPropertiesXml, then deletes them.

conflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a property whose name already exists in its group.
"""
import aclib

group = 'Tapir Example Import'
xml = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no" ?>
<BuildingInformation>
    <PropertyDefinitionGroups>
        <PropertyDefinitionGroup>
            <Name>{group}</Name>
            <Description/>
            <PropertyDefinitions>
                <PropertyDefinition>
                    <Name>Imported Text</Name>
                    <Description/>
                    <ValueDescriptor Type="SingleValueDescriptor">
                        <ValueType>String</ValueType>
                    </ValueDescriptor>
                    <MeasureType>Default</MeasureType>
                    <DefaultValue>
                        <DefaultValueType>Basic</DefaultValueType>
                        <Variant Type="StringVariant">
                            <Status>Normal</Status>
                            <Value>-</Value>
                        </Variant>
                    </DefaultValue>
                    <ClassificationIDs/>
                </PropertyDefinition>
            </PropertyDefinitions>
        </PropertyDefinitionGroup>
    </PropertyDefinitionGroups>
</BuildingInformation>
'''.format (group = group)

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportPropertiesXml', {'xml': xml, 'conflictPolicy': 'skip'})
aclib.PrintJson (result)

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeletePropertyDefinitions', {'propertyIds': [{'propertyId': p} for p in result.get ('created', [])]})
groups = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['propertyGroups']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeletePropertyGroups', {'propertyGroupIds': [{'propertyGroupId': g['propertyGroupId']} for g in groups if g['name'] == group]})

example.code:
"""Makes a custom property available for the first Wall with MakePropertyAvailableForElements, then unavailable again.

Needs a Wall and a custom property that is not available for it. Requires Archicad 25, 26 or 27.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
customProperties = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllProperties', {'propertyTypes': ['Custom'], 'includeAvailability': False})['properties']
values = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyValuesOfElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'properties': [{'propertyId': p['propertyId']} for p in customProperties],
    'includeAvailability': True
})['propertyValuesForElements'][0]['propertyValues']
propertyId = next ((p['propertyId'] for p, value in zip (customProperties, values) if value.get ('isAvailable') is False), None)
if propertyId is None:
    raise SystemExit ('No custom property that is unavailable for the wall.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MakePropertyAvailableForElements', {'elements': walls, 'propertyId': propertyId}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetPropertyValuesOfElements', {'elements': walls, 'properties': [{'propertyId': propertyId}], 'includeAvailability': True})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MakePropertyUnavailableForElements', {'elements': walls, 'propertyId': propertyId})

import aclib

systemId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllClassificationSystems')['classificationSystems'][0]['classificationSystemId']
item = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetAllClassificationsInSystem', {'classificationSystemId': systemId})['classificationItems'][0]['classificationItem']
if item.get ('children'):
    item = item['children'][0]['classificationItem']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetClassificationItemParents', {
    'classificationItemIds': [{'classificationItemId': item['classificationItemId']}]
}))

commands.name: ImportClassificationsXml
commands.description: Imports a Classification Manager XML export, with the given policies for systems and items that already exist. Returns the systems and items it created and removed.

xml.description: A Classification Manager export (XML) to import.

example.description: Imports a small classification system from Classification Manager XML with ImportClassificationsXml, then deletes it. systemConflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a system whose name already exists.
example.code:
"""Imports a small classification system from Classification Manager XML with ImportClassificationsXml, then deletes it.

systemConflictPolicy 'skip' keeps a system whose name already exists.
"""
import aclib

system = 'Tapir Example Import System'
xml = '''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no" ?>
<BuildingInformation>
    <Classification>
        <System>
            <Name>{system}</Name>
            <EditionVersion>1</EditionVersion>
            <EditionDate>
                <Year>2026</Year>
                <Month>1</Month>
                <Day>1</Day>
            </EditionDate>
            <Description/>
            <Source/>
            <Items>
                <Item>
                    <ID>10</ID>
                    <Name>Walls</Name>
                    <Description/>
                    <Children>
                        <Item>
                            <ID>10.1</ID>
                            <Name>External walls</Name>
                            <Description/>
                            <Children/>
                        </Item>
                    </Children>
                </Item>
            </Items>
        </System>
    </Classification>
</BuildingInformation>
'''.format (system = system)

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ImportClassificationsXml', {
    'xml': xml,
    'systemConflictPolicy': 'skip',
    'itemConflictPolicy': 'skip'
}))

systems = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllClassificationSystems')['classificationSystems']
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteClassificationSystems', {
    'classificationSystemIds': [{'classificationSystemId': s['classificationSystemId']} for s in systems if s['name'] == system]
})

commands.name: GetClassificationItemVisibility
commands.description: Tells whether the given classification items are visible (offered) for the given elements, element tool defaults and attributes, such as building materials. Non-existing targets and classification items are reported as errors. Visibility does not tell whether the target is classified with the item, and an item can be visible even if its parent item is not.

targets.description: The elements, element tool defaults and attributes to check the classification items for.

elementType.description: The tool default of this element type is checked.

classificationItemVisibilities.description: One entry per target, in the order of the input. A non-existing element or attribute, or an invalid element type, is represented by an error object.

visibilities.description: One entry per classification item, in the order of the input. A non-existing classification item is represented by an error object.

isVisible.description: Whether the classification item is visible (offered) for the target, as Archicad reports it. It can be true even if a parent item is not visible. It does not tell whether the target is classified with the item.

example.description: Tells whether the first item of the first classification system is offered for the first Wall, the Wall tool default and the first Building Material with GetClassificationItemVisibility. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Tells whether the first item of the first classification system is offered for the first Wall, the Wall tool default and the first Building Material with GetClassificationItemVisibility.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:1]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')
buildingMaterial = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAttributesByType', {'attributeType': 'BuildingMaterial'})['attributes'][0]
systemId = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAllClassificationSystems')['classificationSystems'][0]['classificationSystemId']
item = aclib.RunCommand ('API.GetAllClassificationsInSystem', {'classificationSystemId': systemId})['classificationItems'][0]['classificationItem']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetClassificationItemVisibility', {
    'targets': [
        {'elementId': walls[0]['elementId']},
        {'elementType': 'Wall'},
        {'attributeId': buildingMaterial['attributeId']}
    ],
    'classificationItemIds': [{'classificationItemId': item['classificationItemId']}]
}))

commands.name: CreateProfiles
commands.description: Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters.

profileDataArray.description: Array of data to create new Profiles.

items.description: Data to create or modify a Profile. Its geometry (the cross-section shape) comes from sourceAttributeId (an existing Profile's geometry, copied), from newSkins (AC27+ only, caller-supplied polygon geometry), or both combined. When creating a brand-new Profile (overwriteExisting false, or true but no existing match), at least one of the two must be given. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, both are optional - the existing Profile's own current geometry is preserved by default (e.g. to change only wallType, or to add newSkins on top of the unchanged existing shape). skinOverrides and newSkins' edgeOverrides target skins/edges by the identifiers/indices GetProfiles reports.

attributeId.description: Indentifier of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

index.description: Index of the existing Profile to overwrite, ignored if overwriteExisting is false.

name.description: Name. If overwriteExisting is true, then the existing Profile with the given name will be overwritten.

sourceAttributeId.description: Identifier of an existing Profile whose geometry (cross-section shape) will be copied as the starting point. Optional if newSkins is given: omit it to build the Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins instead of copying anything (AC27+ only).

wallType.description: Profile available for walls. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

beamType.description: Profile available for beams. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

coluType.description: Profile available for columns. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

handrailType.description: Profile available for handrails. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

otherGDLObjectType.description: Profile available for other GDL based objects. Defaults to the source Profile's value.

skinOverrides.description: Modifications to apply to specific skins of the copied geometry, e.g. to change a skin's building material without rebuilding the profile's shape. Each skinId comes from a prior GetProfiles call's skins[].skinId on the source Profile (or, when overwriteExisting is true, on the Profile being overwritten).

skinId.description: Identifies which skin to modify, from GetProfiles' skins[].skinId.

edgeOverrides.description: Modifications to specific edges of this skin, targeted by their position (0-based) in GetProfiles' skins[].edges.

newSkins.description: AC27+ only. Adds brand-new skins built from caller-supplied polygon geometry, instead of (or in addition to) whatever was copied from sourceAttributeId. Combine with sourceAttributeId to add skins to a copied Profile, or omit sourceAttributeId to build a Profile's geometry entirely from newSkins.

replaceSkins.description: AC27+ only. When overwriteExisting targets an existing Profile, discard every one of its existing skins (and any sourceAttributeId geometry given alongside it) before applying newSkins, instead of adding newSkins on top of the preserved existing geometry. Use this to fully replace a Profile's cross-section with a caller-authored shape while keeping its guid and scalar fields (wallType etc.) - e.g. to sync a Profile's geometry from another project, where sourceAttributeId can't be used because it only resolves within the same file. Also discards any existing profileModifiers, since those are tied to the specific geometry being replaced. Ignored when creating a brand-new Profile (there is nothing to discard yet).

overwriteExisting.description: Overwrite the Profile if exists with the same name, or if index is given with the same index. The default is false.
