example.description: Creates a keynote item and prints the autotext tokens that reference its fields, with GetKeynoteAutoTexts. Deletes the keynote item at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a keynote item and prints the autotext tokens that reference its fields, with GetKeynoteAutoTexts.

Deletes the keynote item at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

item = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteItems', {
    'itemsData': [{'key': 'TAPIR-01', 'title': 'Tapir Example Keynote'}]
})['keynoteItemIdsOrErrors'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetKeynoteAutoTexts', {'keynoteItems': [{'keynoteItemId': item['keynoteItemId']}]}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteKeynoteItems', {'keynoteItemIds': [{'keynoteItemId': item['keynoteItemId']}]})

commands.name: CreateKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Creates keynote folders under the given parent folders (or under the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.

foldersData.description: Array of data to create keynote folders.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

example.description: Creates a keynote folder with a subfolder in it, using CreateKeynoteFolders. Deletes the folders at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a keynote folder with a subfolder in it, using CreateKeynoteFolders.

Deletes the folders at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteFolders', {
    'foldersData': [{'key': 'TAPIR', 'title': 'Tapir Example Folder'}]
})['keynoteFolderIdsOrErrors'][0]
aclib.PrintJson (folder)

# Without parentFolderId the folder is created in the root folder.
aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteFolders', {
    'foldersData': [{'parentFolderId': folder['keynoteFolderId'], 'key': 'TAPIR-SUB', 'title': 'Tapir Example Subfolder'}]
}))

# Deleting a folder deletes its content too.
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteKeynoteFolders', {'keynoteFolderIds': [{'keynoteFolderId': folder['keynoteFolderId']}]})

commands.name: CreateKeynoteItems
commands.description: Creates keynote items in the given parent folders (or in the root folder). Available from Archicad 28.

itemsData.description: Array of data to create keynote items.

parentFolderId.description: The parent folder. Optional; defaults to the root folder.

example.description: Creates a keynote folder with a keynote item in it, using CreateKeynoteItems. Deletes the folder and the item at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Modifies the key, title or reference of the given keynote folders. Available from Archicad 28.

foldersData.description: Array of data to modify keynote folders. Only provided fields are changed.

example.description: Creates a keynote folder and changes its title with ModifyKeynoteFolders. Deletes the folder at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyKeynoteItems
commands.description: Modifies the key, title, description or reference of the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.

itemsData.description: Array of data to modify keynote items. Only provided fields are changed.

example.description: Creates a keynote item and changes its title and description with ModifyKeynoteItems. Deletes the item at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: DeleteKeynoteFolders
commands.description: Deletes the given keynote folders including their content. Available from Archicad 28.

example.description: Creates a keynote folder and deletes it with DeleteKeynoteFolders. Deleting a folder deletes its content too. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a keynote folder and deletes it with DeleteKeynoteFolders.

Deleting a folder deletes its content too. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

folder = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteFolders', {
    'foldersData': [{'key': 'TAPIR', 'title': 'Tapir Example Folder'}]
})['keynoteFolderIdsOrErrors'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteKeynoteFolders', {'keynoteFolderIds': [{'keynoteFolderId': folder['keynoteFolderId']}]}))

commands.name: DeleteKeynoteItems
commands.description: Deletes the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28.

example.description: Creates a keynote item and deletes it with DeleteKeynoteItems. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Creates a keynote item and deletes it with DeleteKeynoteItems.

Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

item = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateKeynoteItems', {
    'itemsData': [{'key': 'TAPIR-01', 'title': 'Tapir Example Keynote'}]
})['keynoteItemIdsOrErrors'][0]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteKeynoteItems', {'keynoteItemIds': [{'keynoteItemId': item['keynoteItemId']}]}))

commands.name: CreateKeynoteLabels
commands.description: Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28.

labelsData.description: Array of data to create keynote labels.

position.description: The reference point of the label.

contentFields.description: The keynote fields to include in the label text as autotext. Optional; defaults to all fields.

example.description: Creates a keynote item and places a Label showing its key and title with CreateKeynoteLabels. Deletes the label and the keynote item at the end. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetProjectDataKeys
commands.description: Lists the project data stored by Tapir in the project: the names, the identifiers of the add-on objects that store them, whether they are kept on this client only and the Teamwork user who has reserved them. Project data is text (for example JSON) saved in the project file by scripts and Grasshopper definitions, such as their settings or the mapping of elements to an external system.

keys.description: The project data stored by Tapir in the project.

name.description: The name of the project data.

guid.description: The identifier of the add-on object that stores the project data.

clientOnly.description: True when the project data is kept on this client only and is not shared in Teamwork.

teamworkOwner.description: The Teamwork user who has reserved the project data. Omitted when nobody has reserved it or the project is not a Teamwork project.

example.description: Prints the names of the project data stored by Tapir, with their Teamwork owners, with GetProjectDataKeys.
example.code:
"""Prints the names of the project data stored by Tapir, with their Teamwork owners, with GetProjectDataKeys."""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys'))

commands.name: GetProjectData
commands.description: Gets the content of the project data with the given names.

names.description: The names of the project data to get.

values.description: The project data in the order of the given names, or an error for a name that has no project data.

name.description: The name of the project data.

content.description: The content of the project data.

example.description: Prints the content of every project data stored by Tapir with GetProjectData.
example.code:
"""Prints the content of every project data stored by Tapir with GetProjectData."""
import aclib

keys = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')['keys']
if not keys:
    raise SystemExit ('No project data in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectData', {'names': [k['name'] for k in keys]}))

commands.name: SetProjectData
commands.description: Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

values.description: The project data to create or to overwrite. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so different scripts do not overwrite each other's data.

name.description: The name of the project data.

content.description: The content of the project data, for example a JSON string.

clientOnly.description: Creates the project data on this client only, it is not shared in Teamwork. Used only when the project data is created. The default is false.

unique.description: Creates the project data as a unique add-on object: in Teamwork only one can exist with its name, even when several users create it at the same time. Used only when the project data is created, and cannot be combined with clientOnly. The default is false.

example.description: Saves a JSON text in the project under a name with SetProjectData, reads it back, then deletes it.

commands.name: DeleteProjectData
commands.description: Deletes the project data with the given names.

names.description: The names of the project data to delete.

example.description: Saves a project data and deletes it again with DeleteProjectData.
example.code:
"""Saves a project data and deletes it again with DeleteProjectData."""
import aclib

name = 'tapir-example/to-delete'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'temporary'}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectData', {'names': [name]}))

commands.name: ReserveProjectData
commands.description: Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it.

names.description: The names of the project data to reserve.

conflicts.description: The project data that could not be reserved because another user has reserved it.

name.description: The name of the project data.

example.description: Saves a project data, reserves it in Teamwork with ReserveProjectData, then releases and deletes it. Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation fails.
example.code:
"""Saves a project data, reserves it in Teamwork with ReserveProjectData, then releases and deletes it.

Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation fails.
"""
import aclib

name = 'tapir-example/teamwork'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'shared'}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveProjectData', {'names': [name]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseProjectData', {'names': [name]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectData', {'names': [name]})

commands.name: ReleaseProjectData
commands.description: Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork.

names.description: The names of the project data to release.

example.description: Saves and reserves a project data, then releases it in Teamwork with ReleaseProjectData and deletes it. Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation and the release fail.
example.code:
"""Saves and reserves a project data, then releases it in Teamwork with ReleaseProjectData and deletes it.

Needs a Teamwork project; in a solo project the reservation and the release fail.
"""
import aclib

name = 'tapir-example/teamwork'
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'shared'}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveProjectData', {'names': [name]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReleaseProjectData', {'names': [name]}))
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteProjectData', {'names': [name]})

commands.name: RequestProjectData
commands.description: Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message.

names.description: The names of the project data to request from the users who have reserved them.

mailText.description: The message sent with the request. The default is empty.

example.description: Requests the project data reserved by other Teamwork users from them, with a message, with RequestProjectData. Needs a Teamwork project. Sends the request to the users who reserved the data.
example.code:
"""Requests the project data reserved by other Teamwork users from them, with a message, with RequestProjectData.

Needs a Teamwork project. Sends the request to the users who reserved the data.
"""
import aclib

keys = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetProjectDataKeys')['keys']
reserved = [k['name'] for k in keys if 'teamworkOwner' in k]
if not reserved:
    raise SystemExit ('No reserved project data.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RequestProjectData', {
    'names': reserved,
    'mailText': 'Please release the Tapir project data.'
}))

commands.name: GrantProjectData
commands.description: Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user.

names.description: The names of the project data, reserved by the current user, to grant.

toUserId.description: The Teamwork user id of the user who gets the project data, for example the userId of a user returned by GetProjectDataKeys or ReserveProjectData.

example.description: Saves and reserves a project data, then grants it to another Teamwork user with GrantProjectData. Needs a Teamwork project. Set toUserId to the user to grant to, e.g. the userId of a teamworkOwner that GetProjectDataKeys lists.
example.code:
"""Saves and reserves a project data, then grants it to another Teamwork user with GrantProjectData.

Needs a Teamwork project. Set toUserId to the user to grant to, e.g. the userId of a teamworkOwner
that GetProjectDataKeys lists.
"""
import aclib

toUserId = 2
name = 'tapir-example/teamwork'

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('SetProjectData', {'values': [{'name': name, 'content': 'shared'}]})
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ReserveProjectData', {'names': [name]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GrantProjectData', {'names': [name], 'toUserId': toUserId}))

commands.name: GetMEPElements
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project, optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28.

elementTypes.description: Optional filter for the MEP element types.

domains.description: Optional filter for the MEP domains.

elements.description: The MEP elements.

example.description: Lists the duct and pipe routes and terminals of the project with GetMEPElements. Leave out both filters to list every MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Lists the duct and pipe routes and terminals of the project with GetMEPElements.

Leave out both filters to list every MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPElements', {
    'elementTypes': ['RoutingElement', 'Terminal'],
    'domains': ['Ventilation', 'Piping']
}))

commands.name: GetMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, the floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, preferred transition placement, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28.

example.description: Prints the polyline, segments and nodes of the first MEP routes of the project with GetMEPRoutingElements. Needs at least one MEP route (duct, pipe or cable carrier). Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPPorts
commands.description: Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size, connection status and connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, the nominal size of piping ports (from Archicad 30), and the outer diameter, wall thickness and flange size (Archicad 30) of piping and ventilation ports. Available from Archicad 28.

example.description: Prints the ports of the first MEP elements of the project with GetMEPPorts. Needs at least one MEP element. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPDistributionSystems
commands.description: Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute and member elements. Available from Archicad 28.

distributionSystems.description: The distribution systems of the project.

ports.description: The ports in the distribution systems graph (see GetMEPPorts).

example.description: Prints the MEP distribution systems of the project and their element trees with GetMEPDistributionSystems. The physical systems of a distribution system are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the MEP distribution systems of the project and their element trees with GetMEPDistributionSystems.

The physical systems of a distribution system are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

systems = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPDistributionSystems', {'includeTree': True})['distributionSystems']
for system in systems:
    print (f"{system['domain']} system: {len (system['elements'])} element(s)")
    for node in system.get ('tree', []):
        print (f"{'  ' * (node['depth'] + 1)}{node['elementId']['guid']}")

commands.name: CreateMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP routing elements.

nodeCoordinates.description: The corner points of the route polyline.

crossSectionWidth.description: Optional cross section width applied to all segments.

crossSectionHeight.description: Optional cross section height applied to all segments.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: Optional cross section reference id of the segment preference table (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table of the current routing tool default.

preferenceTableId.description: Optional guid of the segment preference table (see GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.

layerIndex.description: Optional layer attribute index of the routing element and all its parts (routing segments, rigid segments, elbows and transitions). Only a positive index takes effect; otherwise the routing tool default layer is used. A layer that does not exist or is locked gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

defaults.description: Optional changes to the routing tool default of the domain before the route is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the routing tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

routingNode.description: The routing node default: the elbows and transitions placed at the nodes of the route. Available from Archicad 29.

preferenceTableId.description: The guid of an elbow preference table of the domain (see GetMEPPreferenceTables with includeFittingTables).

factorRadius.description: The radius factor of the elbows placed at the nodes.

preferenceTableId.description: The guid of a transition preference table of the domain (see GetMEPPreferenceTables with includeFittingTables).

example.description: Creates a rectangular duct route with one corner and a circular pipe route with CreateMEPRoutingElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: CreateMEPElements
commands.description: Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions, optionally with a changed insulation that applies only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28.

elementsData.description: Array of data to create MEP elements.

domain.description: Required for all types except Equipment.

orientationDirection.description: Optional direction vector of the orientation. Defaults to (1, 0, 0).

orientationRotation.description: Optional rotation vector of the orientation. Defaults to (0, 1, 0).

defaults.description: Optional changes to the tool default before the element is placed. Only what is placed changes, not the tool's settings. A value that cannot be set gives an error for the item, and nothing is placed.

removeInsulation.description: If true, the element is placed without insulation. Cannot be combined with insulationThickness.

example.description: Places a duct terminal and a pipe accessory with the current tool settings using CreateMEPElements. Coordinates are in meters. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPRoutingElements
commands.description: Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, and node positions. Available from Archicad 28.

routingElementsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP routing elements. Only provided fields are changed.

crossSectionWidth.description: New cross section width applied to all segments.

crossSectionHeight.description: New cross section height applied to all segments.

crossSectionShape.description: The new shape is applied to all segments.

crossSectionReferenceId.description: New cross section reference id of the segment preference table applied to all segments (used for circular cross sections). Resolved against preferenceTableId if given, otherwise against the table the segments already use.

preferenceTableId.description: New segment preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) applied to all segments. Not applicable to the CableCarrier domain.

branchPreferenceTableId.description: New branch preference table (guid as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables) of the routing element.

anchor.description: New anchor point of the cross section, on a 3x3 grid, applied to all segments.

referenceLineOffsetX.description: New horizontal offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.

referenceLineOffsetY.description: New vertical offset of the reference line from the anchor point, applied to all segments.

wallThickness.description: New wall thickness applied to all segments.

flangeSize.description: New flange size applied to all segments.

connectionStyle.description: New connection style applied to all segments.

preferredTransitionPlacement.description: New preferred transition placement applied to all nodes.

cutPlanePosition.description: New cut plane position of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.

floorPlanDisplayOption.description: New floor plan display option of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.

showProjection.description: New show projection setting of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.

onStoryVisibility.description: New on-story visibility of the routing element. Available from Archicad 29.

nodePositions.description: New positions of the routing nodes. The size must match the number of nodes of the route.

example.description: Changes the cross section and insulation of a duct route with ModifyMEPRoutingElements. Creates a temporary duct route, modifies it, reads it back and deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ModifyMEPPorts
commands.description: Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28.

portsData.description: Array of data to modify MEP ports. Only provided fields are changed.

portId.description: The port to modify, as returned by GetMEPPorts.

connectionStyle.description: New connection style of the port. Available from Archicad 30.

flowDirection.description: New flow direction of a piping or ventilation port.

outerDiameter.description: New outer diameter of a piping port.

nominalSize.description: New nominal size of a piping port. Available from Archicad 30.

example.description: Changes the flow direction and outer diameter of a pipe port with ModifyMEPPorts. Creates a temporary pipe route, modifies the port at its start, reads it back and deletes the route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: ConnectMEPElements
commands.description: Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27.

connectToId.description: The MEP element or routing element to connect to.

example.description: Connects a branch duct to the middle of a main duct with ConnectMEPElements, which creates a branch element. Creates the two duct routes; the branch starts on the main route, as the command needs. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: CheckMEPPortConnectability
commands.description: Checks whether MEP ports can be connected to other ports, for the given pairs of ports. Archicad 28 and later check the physical connection. Available from Archicad 27.

portPairs.description: The pairs of ports to check.

portId.description: The port to check, as returned by GetMEPPorts.

otherPortId.description: The port to connect it to, as returned by GetMEPPorts.

results.description: The result for each pair of ports, in the order of the input.

isConnectable.description: Whether the port can be connected to the other port.

example.description: Checks with CheckMEPPortConnectability whether the end port of one duct can be connected to the ports of another. Creates two temporary duct routes that meet at one point and deletes them at the end. The command itself works from Archicad 27; creating the routes requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTables
commands.description: Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, wall thickness, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables, plus the rectangular duct tables of the Ventilation domain or the segment tables of the CableCarrier domain. Each table has its name and whether it is editable; the segment tables also have their segmentation lengths from Archicad 29. The rows of the circular, elbow, branch and transition tables say whether they are valid, and the reference set and the angle set say which of their reference ids and angles are defined. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Every row has its index in the table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Available from Archicad 28.

includeFittingTables.description: Also return the elbow, branch and transition preference tables. Defaults to false. Ignored for the CableCarrier domain.

tables.description: The circular segment preference tables of the domain. Empty for the CableCarrier domain.

rectangularTables.description: The rectangular segment preference tables of the Ventilation domain.

cableCarrierTables.description: The segment preference tables of the CableCarrier domain.

referenceSet.description: The reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain. Not returned for the CableCarrier domain.

elbowTables.description: The elbow preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.

branchTables.description: The branch preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true.

transitionTables.description: The transition preference tables of the domain. Only when includeFittingTables is true, available from Archicad 29.

example.description: Prints the pipe preference tables of the project, with the elbow, branch and transition tables, using GetMEPPreferenceTables. The angle set and the transition tables are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the pipe preference tables of the project, with the elbow, branch and transition tables, using GetMEPPreferenceTables.

The angle set and the transition tables are returned from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {
    'domain': 'Piping',
    'includeFittingTables': True
}))

commands.name: ModifyMEPPreferenceTables
commands.description: Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, and deletes reference ids from the reference set and angles from the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28.

tablesToAdd.description: New tables to add to the domain, before the other changes.

tables.description: The tables of the domain to change, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Each table is changed in one undoable step.

tablesToDelete.description: The guids of the tables of the domain to delete, after the other table changes.

referenceIdsToDelete.description: Reference ids to delete from the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain.

anglesToDelete.description: Angles to delete from the angle set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them. Available from Archicad 29.

addedTables.description: One item for each item of tablesToAdd: the guid of the new table, or the error.

tables.description: One result for each item of tables.

deletedTables.description: One result for each item of tablesToDelete.

example.description: Adds a cable carrier segment table, renames it and fills it with rows using ModifyMEPPreferenceTables, then deletes it. Requires Archicad 28 or later.

commands.name: GetMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, editable flag, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroups.description: The system groups of the project with their physical systems.

example.description: Lists the MEP system groups of the project and their physical systems with GetMEPSystemGroups. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Lists the MEP system groups of the project and their physical systems with GetMEPSystemGroups.

Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

for systemGroup in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPSystemGroups', {})['systemGroups']:
    if 'error' in systemGroup:
        continue
    print (f"{systemGroup['name']}: {', '.join (s['name'] for s in systemGroup['physicalSystems'] if 'name' in s)}")

commands.name: CreateMEPSystemGroups
commands.description: Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29.

systemGroupsData.description: Array of data to create system groups.

commands.name: GetMEPRoutingParameters
commands.description: Gets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: of a routing element its routing node parameters (preferred transition placement, elbow from Archicad 29, transition) and routing segment parameters (cross section, preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style); of a routing node its elbow (from Archicad 29) and transition parameters; of a routing segment its rigid segment parameters (Archicad 28 only). Available from Archicad 28.

elements.description: MEP routing elements, routing nodes or routing segments.

routingParameters.description: The routing parameters of the given elements, in their order.

routingNodeParameters.description: The routing node default parameters of a routing element (RoutingElement::GetRoutingNodeDefaultParameters). The elbow is given from Archicad 29.

transition.description: Transition parameters. preferenceTableId is given from Archicad 29.

routingSegmentParameters.description: The routing segment default parameters of the routing element (RoutingElement::GetRoutingSegmentDefaultParameters).

transitionParameters.description: Transition parameters. preferenceTableId is given from Archicad 29.

rigidSegmentParameters.description: The rigid segment default parameters of a routing segment (RoutingSegment::GetRigidSegmentDefaultParameters). Archicad 28 only.

example.description: Prints the routing parameters of the first MEP route of the project and of its nodes and segments with GetMEPRoutingParameters. Needs at least one MEP route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
example.code:
"""Prints the routing parameters of the first MEP route of the project and of its nodes and segments with GetMEPRoutingParameters.

Needs at least one MEP route. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
"""
import aclib

routes = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPElements', {'elementTypes': ['RoutingElement']})['elements']
if not routes:
    raise SystemExit ('No MEP route in the project.')
routeId = routes[0]['elementId']

route = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPRoutingElements', {'elements': [{'elementId': routeId}]})['routingElements'][0]
ids = [routeId] + [node['elementId'] for node in route['nodes']] + [segment['elementId'] for segment in route['segments']]

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPRoutingParameters', {
    'elements': [{'elementId': id} for id in ids]
}))

Only the given keys are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element. Available from Archicad 28.

elbowParameters.description: The elbow parameters of a routing node (RoutingNode::Modifier::SetElbowDefaultParameters). Archicad 29 or newer.

"""Prints every electrical panel of the project with its circuits and loads using GetElectricalPanels.

commands.name: GetMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Gets rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle): whether the row is valid and its values (diameters, wall thickness, radius, length, angle, branch offset, connection length, description), and whether the table exists. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables only give whether they exist, as their rows have no key. On Archicad 27, which has one kind of preference table, a row is found by its shape and index and has a value and a description; the table's name and number of rows per shape are returned too. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

keys.description: The keys of the rows to get.

items.description: The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).

shape.description: Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.

index.description: Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.

name.description: Archicad 27 only: the name of the table.

sizes.description: Archicad 27 only: the number of rows of each shape.

rows.description: The rows in the order of the keys.

key.description: The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).

shape.description: Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.

index.description: Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.

valid.description: Whether the row is valid. Archicad 27: whether the list of the shape has a row with the index.

values.description: The values of a row, lengths in meters. Segment tables: diameter, wallThickness and description. Elbow tables: diameter, radius and description. Branch tables: mainAxisDiameter, branchAxisDiameter, length, branchOffset, connectionLength and description. Pipe transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, length and description. Duct transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, angle and description. Archicad 27: value and description.

value.description: Archicad 27 only: the value of the row.

example.description: Reads the first two rows of the first pipe segment preference table by their reference id with GetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the keys are a shape and an index).
example.code:
"""Reads the first two rows of the first pipe segment preference table by their reference id with GetMEPPreferenceTableRows.

Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the keys are a shape and an index).
"""
import aclib

tables = [t for t in aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {'domain': 'Piping'})['tables'] if t['rows']]
if not tables:
    raise SystemExit ('No pipe segment preference table with rows in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTableRows', {
    'tableId': {'guid': tables[0]['guid']},
    'keys': [{'referenceId': row['referenceId']} for row in tables[0]['rows'][:2]]
}))

commands.name: SetMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Sets the given values of rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table, found by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle). Only the given values are changed, in one undo step. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index, its value and description are set, and its index after the call is returned; the keys give the indices before the call. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

rows.description: The rows to change. Only the given values are set.

key.description: The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).

shape.description: Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.

index.description: Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.

values.description: The values of a row, lengths in meters. Segment tables: diameter, wallThickness and description. Elbow tables: diameter, radius and description. Branch tables: mainAxisDiameter, branchAxisDiameter, length, branchOffset, connectionLength and description. Pipe transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, length and description. Duct transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, angle and description. Archicad 27: value and description.

value.description: Archicad 27 only: the value of the row.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

index.description: Archicad 27 only: the index of the row after the call, which can differ from the index of its key when setting a value moves rows. The keys are the indices before the call.

example.description: Changes the description of a row of an editable pipe segment preference table with SetMEPPreferenceTableRows. Reads the row, changes it, reads it back and restores the old description. Requires Archicad 28 or later (on Archicad 27 the key is a shape and an index).

commands.name: AddMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Adds rows with the given keys and optionally values to a branch, elbow or transition preference table and returns their index, in one undo step. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29; segment tables have a row for each reference id. On Archicad 27 a row is added to the list of the given shape of any preference table, and the index of each new row after the call is returned. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

rows.description: The rows to add, with their key and optionally their values. Branch tables from Archicad 28, elbow and transition tables from Archicad 29. Segment tables have a row for each reference id, so no row can be added to them. Archicad 27: the key has the shape only, the table gives the index.

key.description: The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).

shape.description: Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.

index.description: Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.

values.description: The values of a row, lengths in meters. Segment tables: diameter, wallThickness and description. Elbow tables: diameter, radius and description. Branch tables: mainAxisDiameter, branchAxisDiameter, length, branchOffset, connectionLength and description. Pipe transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, length and description. Duct transition tables: beginDiameter, endDiameter, angle and description. Archicad 27: value and description.

value.description: Archicad 27 only: the value of the row.

executionResults.description: One result per row, in the order of the rows.

index.description: The index of the new row in the table. Archicad 27: in the list of its shape, after the call.

example.description: Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table with AddMEPPreferenceTableRows. The new row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet; it is deleted again at the end. Elbow rows can be added from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table with AddMEPPreferenceTableRows.

The new row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row
for yet; it is deleted again at the end. Elbow rows can be added from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

preferences = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {'domain': 'Piping', 'includeFittingTables': True})
elbowTables = [t for t in preferences.get ('elbowTables', []) if t.get ('isEditable') and t['rows']]
if not elbowTables:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable pipe elbow preference table with rows in the project.')
table = elbowTables[0]
referenceId = table['rows'][0]['referenceId']
usedAngles = [row.get ('angle') for row in table['rows'] if row['referenceId'] == referenceId]
freeAngles = [angle for angle in preferences['angleSet']['angles'] if angle not in usedAngles]
if not freeAngles:
    raise SystemExit ('Every angle of the angle set has a row already.')
key = {'referenceId': referenceId, 'angle': freeAngles[0]}

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddMEPPreferenceTableRows', {
    'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']},
    'rows': [{'key': key, 'values': {'description': 'Added by Tapir'}}]
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows', {'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']}, 'keys': [key]})

commands.name: DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows
commands.description: Deletes rows of a segment, branch, elbow or (from Archicad 29) transition preference table by their key (the reference ids and, for branch and elbow rows from Archicad 29, the angle), in one undo step. The rows of segment tables, and of the elbow tables of Archicad 28, are emptied instead. On Archicad 27 a row is found by its shape and index. Available from Archicad 27.

tableId.description: The guid of a preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTables (the branch, elbow and transition tables with includeFittingTables): a pipe or circular duct segment table, a branch or elbow table of the Piping or Ventilation domain, or, from Archicad 29, a transition table. Rectangular duct and cable carrier segment tables are found too, but their rows have no key. Archicad 27: any preference table, as returned by GetMEPPreferenceTableContainers.

keys.description: The keys of the rows to delete. Segment tables, and the elbow tables of Archicad 28, have a row for each reference id, which is emptied instead. Archicad 27: the indices are those before the call; the rows are deleted from the highest index down.

items.description: The key of a row. Segment tables: referenceId. Elbow tables: referenceId and angle. Branch tables: mainAxisReferenceId, branchAxisReferenceId and branchAxisAngle. Transition tables: beginReferenceId and endReferenceId. The angles are as GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them; Archicad 28 finds the rows by their reference ids only and rejects a key with an angle. Archicad 27: shape and index (AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: shape only).

shape.description: Archicad 27 only: the shape whose list of values the row is in.

index.description: Archicad 27 only: the index of the row in the list of its shape, from 0.

example.description: Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table and deletes it again with DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows. The row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet. Rows of segment tables are emptied instead of deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
example.code:
"""Adds a row to the first editable pipe elbow preference table and deletes it again with DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows.

The row gets the reference id of the first row and an angle of the angle set that this reference id has no row for yet.
Rows of segment tables are emptied instead of deleted. Requires Archicad 29 or later.
"""
import aclib

preferences = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMEPPreferenceTables', {'domain': 'Piping', 'includeFittingTables': True})
elbowTables = [t for t in preferences.get ('elbowTables', []) if t.get ('isEditable') and t['rows']]
if not elbowTables:
    raise SystemExit ('No editable pipe elbow preference table with rows in the project.')
table = elbowTables[0]
referenceId = table['rows'][0]['referenceId']
usedAngles = [row.get ('angle') for row in table['rows'] if row['referenceId'] == referenceId]
freeAngles = [angle for angle in preferences['angleSet']['angles'] if angle not in usedAngles]
if not freeAngles:
    raise SystemExit ('Every angle of the angle set has a row already.')
key = {'referenceId': referenceId, 'angle': freeAngles[0]}
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('AddMEPPreferenceTableRows', {'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']}, 'rows': [{'key': key}]})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows', {
    'tableId': {'guid': table['guid']},
    'keys': [key]
}))

solidLinks.description: For each input element, the solid links where it acts as target and where it acts as operator.

example.description: Gets the solid element operation links of the first three walls with GetSolidElementLinks, as target and as operator. Needs at least one Wall.
example.code:
"""Gets the solid element operation links of the first three walls with GetSolidElementLinks, as target and as operator.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSolidElementLinks', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: CreateSolidOperations
commands.description: Runs a solid operation (subtraction, intersection, addition) on two morphs and returns the resulting morphs, one item per operation. Unlike CreateSolidElementLinks this is not a link: the target and the operator morph are replaced by the result. Morphs only; the operations run in one undo step.

operations.description: The solid operations to run, each on two morphs. The target and the operator morph are replaced by the resulting morph.

results.description: One item per operation, in the order of the input: the resulting morphs, or an error.

elements.description: The morphs created by the operation.

example.description: Subtracts a small box morph from a bigger one with CreateSolidOperations. Both morphs are created by the script and replaced by the resulting morph, which is deleted at the end.

commands.name: TrimElements
commands.description: Trims construction elements with a roof or shell: the roofs and shells in the list, or one given trimming element with a trim type.

elements.description: The construction elements to trim. Without trimmingElement the roofs and shells among them do the trimming.

trimmingElement.description: Optional. The roof or shell that trims every element in the list.

trimType.description: Used with trimmingElement; defaults to KeepInside.

example.description: Trims two walls to the underside of a roof with TrimElements and reads the trims back. The walls and the roof are created by the script and deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Trims two walls to the underside of a roof with TrimElements and reads the trims back.

The walls and the roof are created by the script and deleted at the end.
"""
import math

import aclib

# Two walls under a pitched roof, created by this script and deleted at the end.
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0},
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0}
]})['elements']
roofs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRoofs', {'roofsData': [{
    'level': 2.7,
    'floorIndex': 0,
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (25.0)}],
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, {'x': 100.0, 'y': 105.0}]
}]})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('TrimElements', {
    'elements': walls,
    'trimmingElement': roofs[0]['elementId'],
    'trimType': 'KeepInside'
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementTrims', {'elements': walls})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls + roofs})

commands.name: RemoveElementTrims
commands.description: Removes the trim between an element and the roof or shell trimming it.

elementPairs.description: The trimmed element and the roof or shell trimming it, per pair.

example.description: Removes the trim between two walls and the roof above them with RemoveElementTrims. The walls, the roof and the trims are created by the script first; the elements are deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Removes the trim between two walls and the roof above them with RemoveElementTrims.

The walls, the roof and the trims are created by the script first; the elements are deleted at the end.
"""
import math

import aclib

# Two walls under a pitched roof, created by this script and deleted at the end.
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateWalls', {'wallsData': [
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0},
    {'begCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, 'endCoordinate': {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, 'height': 4.0, 'floorIndex': 0}
]})['elements']
roofs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateRoofs', {'roofsData': [{
    'level': 2.7,
    'floorIndex': 0,
    'levels': [{'levelHeight': 10.0, 'levelAngle': math.radians (25.0)}],
    'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 100.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 100.0}, {'x': 106.0, 'y': 105.0}, {'x': 100.0, 'y': 105.0}]
}]})['elements']

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('TrimElements', {'elements': walls + roofs})

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('RemoveElementTrims', {
    'elementPairs': [{'elementId': wall['elementId'], 'trimmingElementId': roofs[0]['elementId']} for wall in walls]
}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementTrims', {'elements': walls})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': walls + roofs})

commands.name: GetElementTrims
commands.description: Which roofs and shells trim each queried element, with the trim type, and which elements it trims.

elementTrims.description: One item per queried element, in order. An unknown or deleted element is an error item, so it cannot be mistaken for an element that is simply not trimmed.

example.description: Gets which roofs and shells trim the first three walls with GetElementTrims, and what each wall trims. Needs at least one Wall.

"""Gets which roofs and shells trim the first three walls with GetElementTrims, and what each wall trims.

Needs at least one Wall.
"""
import aclib

walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements'][:3]
if not walls:
    raise SystemExit ('No wall in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementTrims', {'elements': walls}))

commands.name: MergeElements
commands.description: Merges the given construction elements (the Merge command of Archicad, which cleans up the junctions of slabs, beams, walls and similar elements). Undoable. The element types are not filtered: Archicad reports the ones it cannot merge.

elements.description: The construction elements to merge together. At least two.

example.description: Merges two adjacent slabs with MergeElements, the Merge command of Archicad, and reads the merge back. The slabs are created by the script and deleted at the end.
example.code:
"""Merges two adjacent slabs with MergeElements, the Merge command of Archicad, and reads the merge back.

The slabs are created by the script and deleted at the end.
"""
import aclib

# Two adjacent slabs, created by this script and deleted at the end.
slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateSlabs', {
    'slabsData': [
        {'level': 0.0, 'thickness': 0.3, 'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 50.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 54.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 54.0, 'y': 54.0}, {'x': 50.0, 'y': 54.0}]},
        {'level': 0.0, 'thickness': 0.3, 'polygonCoordinates': [{'x': 54.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 56.0, 'y': 50.0}, {'x': 56.0, 'y': 54.0}, {'x': 54.0, 'y': 54.0}]}
    ]
})['elements']

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('MergeElements', {'elements': slabs}))

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMergedElements', {'elements': slabs})

aclib.RunTapirCommand ('DeleteElements', {'elements': slabs})

commands.name: UnmergeElements
commands.description: Removes the merge between the two elements of each given pair. Undoable; one execution result per pair.

elementPairs.description: The pairs of merged elements to separate. The order within a pair does not matter.

example.description: Removes the merge between two slabs with UnmergeElements. The slabs are created and merged by the script first, and deleted at the end.

commands.name: GetMergedElements
commands.description: Gets the elements each queried element is merged with, one item per queried element; an unknown element is an error item.

elementMerges.description: One item per queried element, in order: the elements it is merged with. An unknown or deleted element is an error item, so it cannot be mistaken for an element that is simply not merged.

example.description: Gets the elements each of the first three slabs is merged with using GetMergedElements. Needs at least one Slab.
example.code:
"""Gets the elements each of the first three slabs is merged with using GetMergedElements.

Needs at least one Slab.
"""
import aclib

slabs = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Slab'})['elements'][:3]
if not slabs:
    raise SystemExit ('No slab in the project.')

aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetMergedElements', {'elements': slabs}))

commands.name: ShowScriptUI
commands.description: Shows the given HTML content in a native Archicad palette (a tkinter alternative for Python scripts).

htmlContent.description: The full HTML document to display in the Script UI palette.

width.description: Optional palette client width in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

height.description: Optional palette client height in pixels. Leave unset to keep the current size.

title.description: Optional palette window title. Leave unset to keep the current title.

resizable.description: Whether the user can drag-resize the palette. Defaults to true.

zoomEnabled.description: Whether Ctrl+scroll/pinch zooming is allowed in the page. Defaults to true.

zoomLevel.description: Optional initial zoom level (1.0 = 100%). Leave unset to keep the current zoom.

scrollBarsVisible.description: Whether the browser's own scrollbars are shown. Defaults to true.

contextMenuEnabled.description: Whether right-click shows the browser's context menu (e.g. Inspect Element). Defaults to true.

navigationDisabled.description: Prevents the page from navigating away (e.g. clicking a link to another site) once it has loaded. Defaults to false.

allowSelfSignedCertificates.description: Only relevant if htmlContent links to a remote https:// resource with a self-signed certificate. Defaults to false.

clearCookies.description: Deletes all browser cookies before loading htmlContent. Defaults to false.

autoHeight.description: Automatically resizes the palette's height to fit the page content as it changes. Defaults to false.

example.description: Shows a small HTML page with a button in an Archicad palette with ShowScriptUI. The page sends its result with window.ACAPI.SubmitResult; read it with GetScriptUIResult.
example.code:
"""Shows a small HTML page with a button in an Archicad palette with ShowScriptUI. The page sends its result with window.ACAPI.SubmitResult; read it with GetScriptUIResult. """ import aclib html = """

Hello from Tapir!

""" aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ShowScriptUI', { 'htmlContent': html, 'title': 'Tapir', 'width': 300, 'height': 150, 'resizable': False }))

commands.name: GetScriptUIResult
commands.description: Retrieves and clears the result last submitted from the Script UI palette's page (via window.ACAPI.SubmitResult), if any, and reports whether the palette is still open, so a waiting script can stop when the user closes it.

hasResult.description: True if the Script UI page has submitted a result since the last call.

result.description: The submitted content (as passed to window.ACAPI.SubmitResult). Only present when hasResult is true.

isOpen.description: True while the Script UI palette is open. False before the first ShowScriptUI call and once the user closed the palette with its close box, the page called window.ACAPI.ClosePalette or Archicad closed it; stays true while Archicad only temporarily hides all palettes (e.g. during a modal dialog). Lets a waiting script stop polling when the user closes the palette.

example.description: Shows a palette with two buttons and waits for the user's choice with GetScriptUIResult. Polls until a button is clicked or the palette is closed.
example.code:
"""Shows a palette with two buttons and waits for the user's choice with GetScriptUIResult. Polls until a button is clicked or the palette is closed. """ import time import aclib html = """

Continue?

""" aclib.RunTapirCommand ('ShowScriptUI', {'htmlContent': html, 'title': 'Tapir', 'width': 300, 'height': 150}) while True: response = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetScriptUIResult') if response['hasResult'] or not response['isOpen']: break time.sleep (0.5) print (response.get ('result', 'The palette was closed without an answer.'))
